jobs.title: Retail Inventory Lead, Waterside Shops
jobs.description:
The role of a Retail Store Inventory Lead at Vuori is an essential part of the store leadership team. You take initiative, have strong assessment skills, communicate with your team on all inventory happenings, and are agile at adapting to the ebbs and flows of the day-to-day business. You work closely with the Store Manager and Assistant Manager in providing a great experience for both the team and customers as well as the needs of the business. The Retail Store Inventory Lead is the leader of the inventory program in their store and will manage all inventory related tasks.

What you'll get to do:

Create a dynamic experience for the back of house

• Forge lasting relationships with store managers, team members, and customers.
• Work with the sales team to ensure each customer receives the best service possible.
• Ensure the back room is tidy, and easy to navigate.
• Ensure destock and restock is handled on a daily basis.
• Ensure the back of the house is kept organized.

Be the Business/Operations

• Attend monthly inventory meetings.
• Manage weekly cycle counts.
• Manage store to store transfers.
• Manage weekly manual restocks to ensure the floor is fully stocked.
• Ensure all shipments are being received and processed in a timely manner, and follow up with store managers if needed.
• Identify and communicate product concerns in a timely manner.

Who you are:

• Must be available to work at least one weekend day and some holidays.
• Must adhere to scheduled shifts with punctuality.
• Ability to develop relationships with customers and colleagues.
• Ability to positively and proactively handle customer concerns.
• Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
• Ability to quickly learn new procedures and processes.
• Strong organizational and follow-through skills.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
• High level of ownership, accountability, and initiative.
• Eager to develop new skills and responsive to feedback.

Our investment in you:

At Vuori, we’re proud to offer the following to our employees:

• Health Insurance
• Savings and Retirement Plan
• Employee Assistance Program
• Generous Vuori Discount & Industry Perks
• Paid Time Off
• Wellness & Fitness benefits

The hourly range for this role is $17/hr - $20/hr, plus team pooled commission.

Vuori is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Environmental Technician II
jobs.description:
AECOM has an exciting opportunity for an Environmental Technician II to join our Remediation team in Jacksonville, FL. You will work on a diverse range of projects delivering remediation system solutions to our key clients. This position will involve travel throughout the region on a regular basis.

The successful candidate will have the ability to communicate effectively with members of the project team, clients, site personnel and office management, and work both independently and as part of a project team. In addition, the successful candidate will be committed to the team’s success and growth; will rigorously apply safety policies and procedures; and will effectively manage the quality of field efforts within the bounds of the AECOM Quality Management System.

The role requires a strong mechanical and safety aptitude, and the candidate must have experience working with plumbing, electrical, and general construction related trades.  Duties include (but will not be limited to) equipment maintenance coordination, remediation system maintenance, and environmental sampling activities.  Although this is a field position that involves significant equipment maintenance and construction related activities, there will be direct interaction with clients and the candidate must have experience communicating with clients on a professional level.

The job responsibilities for the position will include but are not limited to the following:.

• Performs a variety of tasks in support of project staff.
• May gather and maintain specified records of scientific data for supervisor, including but not limited to environmental sampling, operations and maintenance and inspections at client sites.
• Other activities may include assisting with calculations, setting up and operating equipment, inspecting equipment and installations for compliance with specifications and maintaining proper project documentation.
• Collects and enters data and applies technical principles and theories under supervision.
• Self-motivated, organized and understands the concepts of environmental remediation projects including soil and groundwater sampling procedures.
• Reports and documents routinely to project managers of field finds and conditions and makes recommendations based on findings.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

• HS + 2 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Experience operating and maintaining soil and groundwater remediation equipment
• Ability to work outdoors, often in inclement weather conditions
• Valid US Driver’s License and as a condition of employment must pass the AECOM Motor Vehicle screening
• As a condition of employment, candidates must pass a drug screening
• As a condition of employment, candidates must pass a medical screening

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS:

• Strong mechanical aptitude and experience with soil and groundwater remediation technologies, design, implementation, and operation/maintenance activities
• Current 40-hr HazWOPER Certification and associated refresher
• Current First Aid, CPR and AED certification
• Strong understanding of project documentation requirements including taking organized and detailed field notes, recording observations

• Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
• Relocation is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Finetuning
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We're looking for a Research Engineer to help make Claude more capable, reliable and useful on complex, real-world work. You'll work across research and engineering, from early ideas and experiments through to improvements in our models.

This is an early-stage team working on open-ended problems. Priorities will change as we learn, and you'll have a lot of ownership over what you work on. We're looking for someone who's excited about that, and who enjoys working closely with both research and product.

Key responsibilities

• Design and run experiments to improve model capabilities

• Build reinforcement learning environments and evaluations

• Develop the tools and infrastructure needed to support this research

• Collaborate with teams across research, engineering and product

• Help shape the direction of a new area of research

Minimum qualifications

• Strong software engineering skills, including proficiency in Python

• Experience training, fine-tuning or evaluating machine learning models

• A track record of owning ambiguous technical projects end to end

• Strong communication skills and a collaborative working style

• Care about the societal impacts and safety of your work

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with reinforcement learning, particularly in long-horizon or sparse-reward settings

• Experience building reinforcement learning environments, simulation systems or large-scale ML infrastructure

• Experience building evaluations or benchmarks for agentic systems

• Experience working closely with product teams to drive model improvements

Representative projects

• Build a simulation where decisions made early on have consequences much later, and use it to train a model

• Design an evaluation for work that takes a long time and has no single right answer

• Investigate where a model's independence breaks down on long projects, and run experiments to improve it

• Develop a way for people to oversee a large amount of work without reviewing every step

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$500,000—$850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Sr. Talent Acquisition Associate
jobs.description:
Our Team

Highspring’s Talent Acquisition team partners with leaders across the enterprise to attract, assess and hire talent that supports our business and clients. We play a critical role in supporting the firm’s continued development and growth. Our collaborative team partners with leaders across the business to help identify, assess and hire individuals with the critical skills and experience our clients need and the entrepreneurial spirit and passion for service that drive our culture.

We are seeking a top performer who can quickly integrate with the team, manage assigned searches and deliver a consistent, high-quality hiring experience in a fast-paced professional services environment. This role offers flexibility to either work remotely or from one of our Highspring office locations. Come be a part of our fun, friendly, flexible, dynamic, diverse, high-performance team!

What Will You Do?

• Partner with Talent Acquisition colleagues, hiring leaders and interview teams across Highspring to understand role requirements, establish recruiting plans and manage assigned searches from intake through offer acceptance.

• Develop targeted sourcing strategies using professional networks, referrals, social media, job boards, industry groups and direct outreach.

• Source passive prospects, manage inbound applicants and make timely disposition decisions based on agreed-upon job requirements.

• Conduct structured screening interviews to assess relevant experience, capabilities, motivations, compensation expectations and alignment with the opportunity.

• Present qualified, interested candidates for roles across Highspring’s business lines and shared services functions, based on the needs of the engagement.

• Coordinate interviews, maintain clear communication with candidates and hiring teams, and support offer development, negotiation and acceptance.

• Build and maintain pipelines for current and anticipated hiring needs, documenting activity and candidate status accurately in Highspring’s recruiting systems.

• Deliver a responsive, professional candidate experience that reflects Highspring’s culture and provides clear, timely information throughout the recruiting process.

• Provide accurate pipeline reporting, identify risks or bottlenecks and support recruiting projects, events and process improvements as needed.

What Do You Need to Succeed?

Minimum Qualifications

• At least 3 years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including responsibility for sourcing, screening, stakeholder management and offer support.

• Demonstrated success recruiting in a corporate, professional services or search firm environment while managing multiple concurrent roles.

• Proven ability to identify and engage passive prospects using a range of sourcing platforms, tools and professional networks.

• Results-oriented approach with the ability to prioritize competing demands, meet deadlines and maintain attention to detail.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment and a service-oriented approach.

• Ability to ramp up quickly, work independently within established processes and collaborate effectively as part of a distributed team.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365, applicant tracking systems, sourcing tools and structured or behavioral interviewing practices.

• Availability to work agreed-upon hours and remain responsive to candidates and stakeholders throughout the temporary assignment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience recruiting talent in professional services and/or management consulting functions.

• Working knowledge of recruiting compliance requirements and hiring best practices.

• Familiarity with one or more of the following talent markets: Consulting and professional services including public accounting/advisory career paths Technology, data and enterprise systems, including IT advisory career paths in ERP systems implementations, data & analytics and CIO advisory services Management Consulting candidate market

jobs.title: Sustainability & Corporate Affairs Manager
jobs.description:
As Sustainability & Corporate Affairs Manager Benelux, you will lead the integrated sustainability and corporate affairs agenda for one of JDE Peet’s’ most strategically important markets. You will translate global and European priorities into clear local strategies, practical business decisions and credible external positioning across the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg. Working closely with local leadership, Sales, Marketing, Legal, HR and Supply Chain, you will help create commercial value while anticipating regulatory, reputational and stakeholder risks. You will build trusted relationships with authorities, industry bodies, NGOs, customers and other external partners, and represent JDE Peet’s in relevant forums and media engagements. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who combines strategic judgement with practical execution and can influence stakeholders locally, across Northern Europe and at global level.

• Shape and execute the integrated Sustainability & Corporate Affairs strategy for the Benelux, translating global and European priorities into relevant local plans and measurable action.
• Act as a strategic partner to local leadership and business functions, embedding sustainability and reputation considerations in customer, commercial and operational decisions.
• Lead high-impact customer support, strategic partnerships, pre-tenders and tenders, turning sustainability priorities into credible propositions and shared-value initiatives.
• Develop stakeholder and advocacy plans, build trusted external relationships and coordinate external communications, media engagement, working visits and reputation-building activities.
• Monitor and translate national and EU developments, guide the business on claims, disclosures, EPR, certifications and reporting, and coordinate early mitigation of regulatory and reputational risks.
• Represent the Benelux towards European and Global teams, sharing market intelligence and implementation insights while promoting local best practices, pilots and innovation across Northern Europe.

Working at JDE Peet’s is hands-on, giving you the chance to leave your mark while working together as one team. We’re a fast-paced company on a mission, focused on what matters most. Our environment demands energy, agility, and bold thinking. If you’re ready to make an impact and grow in a global team, JDE Peet’s is the place for you.

For this role as a Sustainability & Corporate Affairs Manager Benelux, we’re looking for someone who has the following skills and experience:

• A master’s degree, or equivalent relevant experience, in Corporate Affairs, Public Affairs, Sustainability, Business Management or a related discipline.
• At least 7–10 years of relevant experience in an international, fast-paced FMCG business or a similarly complex environment.
• Demonstrable expertise across corporate affairs and several sustainability topics, such as responsible sourcing, human rights, carbon footprint, packaging, circularity, claims, reporting or regulation.
• A proven ability to operate at both strategic and operational levels, translating complex technical or regulatory topics into clear business decisions and credible communication.
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including experience engaging senior leaders, customers, authorities, industry bodies, NGOs or strategic partners without formal authority.
• Fluent in Dutch and business English, excellent written, verbal and public-speaking skills, and a pragmatic, structured and resilient approach in complex situations.

Your application at JDE Peet's

If you are interested in this career opportunity at JDE Peet's, apply and join us. After receiving your application, we will do our utmost to give you quick feedback. Part of the recruitment procedure at JDE Peet's would be an online assessment, followed by interviews. A pre-employment check can be part of the recruitment process.

Our DE&I Statement

At JDE Peet’s we aim to create a better future where we authentically serve, reflect and embrace everyone. We believe in fostering a more diverse, equitable and inclusive organisation where everyone feels comfortable to truly be who they are and unleash their full potential. This means we do not tolerate discrimination on the basis of our race, ethnicity, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, age, disability, or any other trait protected by law.

Throughout the entire employee lifecycle, we place DE&I at the core of our people processes. This enables us to drive objectivity and eliminate any potential bias, ensuring an inclusive experience in the workplace. Do not hesitate to reach out if you require any reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process.

Our efforts on this agenda have earned us the prestigious Catalyst Award, as well as the Fair Pay Leader Certification in 2025 thanks to an unexplained gender pay gap of 0.52%.

JDE Peet’s - now part of Keurig Dr Pepper – is the world’s leading pure-play coffee company, with a presence in more than 100 markets. Guided by our ‘Reignite the Amazing’ strategy, we are focused on brand-led growth across three big bets: Peet’s, L’OR, and our 10 strategically selected local icons led by Jacobs.

jobs.title: Brand Designer
jobs.location: Atlanta, Georgia; Chicago, United States; New York, United States; Remote - Virginia
jobs.description:
About Teneo

Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.

Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other corporations, financial institutions and organizations.

Our full range of advisory services includes strategic communications, investor relations, financial transactions and restructuring, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, organizational design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance, ESG and DE&I.

The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 50+ offices around the world.

Do you want to step into bigger briefs and better work?

The bar we’re setting:

We’re looking for a strong mid-level designer with ideas, sharp craft and the ambition to make good work better.

This is a hands-on role working across brand, campaigns, digital, editorial and social, turning clear thinking into distinctive, beautifully executed design.

You’ll have a strong point of view, an eye for detail and the confidence to develop ideas, not just execute them. You’ll work closely with creative directors, strategists and project teams, taking ownership of your work while getting the direction and support to keep pushing it further.

We’re looking for someone curious, collaborative and proactive. A designer who cares about the work, wants to keep getting better and will help raise the creative standard of the team.

The Role

You’ll help shape brand-led work across identity, campaigns, digital, editorial and social. That includes reports and long-form content where structure, layout and typography matter, as well as social assets where pace, clarity and cut-through are key.

You’ll work closely with creatives, strategists and account teams to interpret briefs, explore design routes and bring ideas to life across a range of channels.

You won’t be expected to lead every project independently, but you should be ready to own defined tasks, manage your time well and present your thinking clearly.

This is a role for a designer with taste, curiosity and momentum — someone who wants to get stuck in, build confidence and make work they’re proud of.

Responsibilities

• Develop creative ideas and design routes in response to B2B briefs.

• Create design work across brand, campaign, digital, editorial, presentation and social channels.

• Support the development of visual identities, campaign concepts and brand systems.

• Design and produce social assets for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and other relevant platforms.

• Apply editorial thinking to reports, presentations, and long-form content.

• Bring brand guidelines to life with consistency and creativity.

• Take defined tasks and smaller projects from brief through to delivery.

• Collaborate with creatives, strategists and account teams.

• Present ideas clearly internally and, where appropriate, support creative presentations to clients.

• Use feedback to refine and strengthen the work.

• Prepare accurate, production-ready files for print, digital, social and presentation use.

• Maintain high standards across typography, layout, image choice, motion and detail.

• Stay curious about design, culture, tools and how AI can support the creative process.

• Bring energy, openness and a willingness to get involved.

Qualifications

• 3-5+ years experience in a design studio, agency or in-house creative team, although we care more about the quality of your portfolio, thinking and craft than an exact number of years.

• A portfolio showing strong visual craft, original thinking and confident work across relevant channels.

• Experience across brand, campaign, digital, social and editorial design.

• Strong typography, layout, hierarchy and visual systems skills.

• Good editorial design skills, particularly across reports, presentations and long-form content.

• Experience creating social assets and adapting ideas across formats.

• Able to develop ideas, not just execute instructions.

• Confident working within brand guidelines.

• Able to explain creative thinking and design choices clearly.

• Good understanding of how design supports communication, brand and business objectives.

• Strong working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite, especially InDesign, Illustrator and Photoshop.

• Strong working knowledge of Figma.

• Animation or motion skills, including After Effects, are welcome.

• Organized, reliable and able to manage multiple tasks.

• Collaborative, proactive and keen to keep learning.

• A positive, willing attitude — someone who wants to lean in, support the team and raise the standard.

About Teneo Studio

Teneo Studio is the in-house creative team, turning complex B2B challenges into clear, compelling ideas across brand, content, campaigns and engagement. The studio is growing into a high-performing, creatively ambitious powerhouse, known for sharp thinking, strong ideas and work that stands out.

jobs.description:
Structural Steel Fitting & Welding Foreman
Location: York, PA
Job Type: Full-Time | Direct Hire
Shift: 2nd Shift
Starting Pay: $39.00/hour; higher depending on experience (up to $42.00/hour)
2nd Shift Differential: Additional $3.00/hour
Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced Structural Steel Fitting & Welding Foreman to lead shop operations and oversee a team of welders and fitters during second shift.
This position is responsible for coordinating daily fabrication activities, assigning work, monitoring production progress, and ensuring all completed work meets quality and delivery requirements. The Foreman will provide hands-on leadership while coordinating with other departments, suppliers, and management to keep operations running efficiently.
The ideal candidate has extensive structural steel fabrication experience, a background supervising welding and fitting personnel, and the ability to manage production schedules, employees, equipment, and materials.

Pay Rate: Up to $32.00/hour, depending on experience

We are looking for a Quality Control Inspector with a background in structural steel fabrication to help maintain product quality throughout the manufacturing process.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION:

At Sunrise Robotics, we are dedicated to augmenting humanity through intelligent robotics. Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.



OUR VISION:

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. Our vision is to integrate flexible robotic solutions, based on generic hardware and advanced software/AI capabilities, into manufacturing, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises, to make automation economically viable and accessible, for all sizes of manufacturers. We are not just building robots; we are creating the strategically crucial components for autonomous, intelligent agents of the future.

The role:

We are hiring a Chief of Staff to the CEO.

You are the CEO's closest execution partner. You sit in the rooms the CEO sits in, and represent him in the ones he cannot be in. You make sure the company executes fast on the decisions made in those rooms, by driving the most important cross-team projects yourself.

The mandate has four parts. Run the operating cadence the leadership team works inside. Own the company's commitments and see them through to done. Make the CEO's decisions and priorities legible to everyone they affect. Protect the CEO's time for the work only the CEO can do.

This is a senior individual role with no direct reports. Your authority comes from the mandate, agreed in writing with the CEO, and from being right. You are not a gatekeeper.

We are outcome-driven, direct, high trust and high autonomy. There is very little hand-holding. We enjoy working with people who bring a healthy degree of intensity and drive.

What this role is not:

Not an executive assistant. Not a COO. Not a strategy seat where you write decks about work other people do.

What you will do:

 - Run the operating cadence
   Own the quarterly planning cycle, company goals and the weekly leadership meeting: agenda, a dashboard of under 15 metrics, decisions written down, commitments tracked to done. Every red metric gets a root cause and an owner within the week.

 - Drive cross-functional execution
   When a decision needs three teams and has no single owner, you are the direct responsible individual until it lands. You hold owners to their dates, unblock, and escalate early. Most of these run in weeks, not quarters.

 - Make decisions travel
   Every leadership decision gets written down and reaches the people it affects within a day. You draft the all-hands deck, decision memos and internal communication in the CEO's voice. The CEO edits; you draft. You hold the bar in the rooms the CEO is not in. When quality or pace drops, you name it that day.

 - Build and manage the operating system
   Morning briefs, commitments tracking, meeting-to-action pipelines, and the reporting the CEO takes to the board. Build the foundation and systems, so the company gets more legible with less manual work. You do this yourself, not through a vendor.

 - Make the company legible
   Decisions, processes and playbooks written once, findable by everyone, and used as the standard.

 - Take special projects, up to a day a week
   You pick them up with CEO-level urgency and hand them back completed, or with an owner and a clear path to done.

Who you are:

 - You bring energy
   High intensity, high pace, and you are impatient when good decisions sit. You set the tempo in a room without raising your voice. People move faster because you are there.

 - You have operated inside a fast-changing, venture-backed company
   Typically four to eight years in. You have lived through at least one moment where the plan changed under you and you kept the team executing. Titles vary: chief of staff, business operations, founder's associate, program or product lead, consultant who went operating, ex-founder. We care about the work, not the title.

 - You build systems, not just tasks
   Somewhere, a team runs on a cadence or a tool you set up, and it kept working after you left the room.

 - You think in systems
   You see how a change in hiring shows up in deploy capacity three months later. You spot the second-order effect before it hits.

 - You run complex projects across stakeholders
   Several teams, outside parties, a hard deadline, no formal authority. You have done that and landed it.

 - You are technically fluent
   Strong technical fluency is required. You are equally at home in a spreadsheet and a database. You pull your own numbers, build your own model, and follow an engineering discussion closely enough to ask the question that matters.

 - You are AI-native
   You have built agents or automations that run without you: a pipeline, a briefing, a tracker. You can show us. Daily use of a chatbot is not enough.

 - You write and visualize information clearly
   Short, clear, and in someone else's voice when needed. A one-page memo from you ends a debate. You turn data into the chart that makes the decision obvious.

 - You chase without being annoying
   Following up daily is the job. People end up grateful you did.

 - You hold confidences
   You will know about sensitive information before almost anyone. That access is a duty, not a way to be liked.

 - You push back
   You get to the real intent behind a vague request and say when we are wrong. You argue from facts.

 - You are curious about the actual work
   You want to know what a deploy engineer does in a customer's facility at 6am, and you go and find out.

Bonus points:

 - You have shipped something with Claude Code, Codex or similar, and can talk about what broke.

 - You have worked in hardware, robotics or manufacturing, where part of the team works next to the machines.

Location:

Remote within Europe. For the first six months you spend up to half your time in Ljubljana, next to the CEO. After that, remote with regular travel to Ljubljana.

Why Sunrise?

 - Work directly with the CEO, founders and leadership at an early stage, in a role that touches every decision the company makes.

 - We care about talent density, speed of execution and long-term technology leverage.

 - Get things done, and you shape your own trajectory.

jobs.title: Staff Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT PLAYLAB

Playlab is a tech non-profit dedicated to helping educators and students become critical consumers and creators of AI.

We believe that an open-source, community-driven approach is key to harnessing the potential of AI in education. We equip educators & students to build custom AI apps for their unique context. Over 100,000 educators have published apps on Playlab.

At Playlab, we believe that AI is a new design material, one that should be shaped by many to bring their ideas about learning to life. If you're passionate about building creative, equitable futures for students and teachers, we hope you'll join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Playlab is looking for a Staff Platform Engineer to build the infrastructure and APIs that let anyone deploy edtech apps that are good and safe for students by default. Every new AI capability, from image generation to agent memory, arrives built for adults and businesses. On Playlab, students and teachers use these capabilities to build their own apps and agents, so each one has to work differently: web search with safety controls a district can tune, memory that doesn't harden into assumptions about a student, storage APIs that understand relationships between people in the school. 

We're adding capabilities Playlab doesn't have yet and breaking the app we grew up as into composable, reusable building blocks for building the next generation of edtech. Our own engineers build on them first, then teammates who don't write code, then educators and students making apps tailored to their own classrooms. You'll join the platform team we're building to shape what those blocks are and lead the design and implementation of key pieces. We're committed to open sourcing our infrastructure over time, so your design decisions will be used well beyond Playlab.

This is a staff level individual contributor role reporting to engineering leadership. You'll stay close to schools and users and work with product, privacy and security, trust and safety, learning engineering, and machine learning to build products and agents on top of your work.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build the building blocks

 - Make powerful capabilities right for education. Build capabilities like agent memory, image generation, and data storage with the shape it needs before it reaches a classroom. You'll design these with product, privacy and security, and trust and safety experts, grounded in what we learn in schools, then build them in so every app and agent gets them by default.

 - Design blocks others can build. You'll play a pivotal role in the team deciding how new core infrastructure works - designing APIs and leading builds, so new features and experiences can be scaffolded on solid foundations.

 - Turn our data into something schools can learn from. Grow our warehouse and data vault into the place where schools and their research partners can answer questions about AI in their classrooms.

 - Ship early and learn. You can expect to ship major new infrastructure in production within your first month, and evolve it as new usage patterns emerge.

Own where agents run

 - Give educators' agents a powerful place to run. A runtime where the agents and apps educators build can use tools, run code and work for hours on a teacher's behalf, safe enough for classrooms by default.

 - Build the infrastructure for educational evaluations. Make it easy to run, store and compare evaluations at scale that help teachers and students understand where the things they build are performing or not, and help the field learn from what they build.

Set the standards and open them up

 - Write the conventions others follow. Create designs and conventions the next several systems are built to and raise the bar for architecture reviews across the team.

 - Build for the commons. Design core infrastructure with a mind towards open sourcing it.




HOW YOU'LL WORK

 - Start from the classroom. Spend time with teachers, students and our learning engineers to see how a capability will actually be used before you design it.

 - Design with the experts. Work each capability through with product, privacy and security, and trust and safety, and write designs that name the options you rejected, so people can push back early.

 - Prototype, then harden. Get a rough version into real hands quickly, learn from it, and decide which experiments earn a permanent place in the platform.

 - Make the team stronger. Project leadership rotates here. Sometimes you'll lead; often you'll make a teammate's project succeed through design, review and pairing.




WHAT THE JOB IS REALLY LIKE

 - Mostly building, some operations. Most of your time goes to designing and building blocks, but a real share goes to Terraform, monitoring, alerts and incidents. You won't be shielded from operations.

 - A platform team that's still forming. You'll join a few engineers already on it, plus a devsecops partner and a new security team. It's still small, so you'll do hands-on work a larger company would spread across several teams.

 - Students are on the other end. These systems serve everything from K-12 classrooms to higher ed to ministries of education during the school day. Outages and data mistakes land on teachers and students, so the bar on isolation, privacy and reliability is higher than our size would suggest.




YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU

You're a systems designer who starts from the people using what you build and still loves to ship. You'd rather make ten engineers faster than be the fastest one yourself, and building for students makes a problem more interesting to you, not less.

 - Have designed several systems that worked together as a platform: shared conventions, consistent APIs, and other teams building on them as usage and requirements changed.

 - Have worked with privacy, safety or policy experts to make their requirements part of the product.

 - Have led a few engineers through building new infrastructure: shaped the design with them, broke it into work, got it to production, and left conventions the team kept using.

 - Are hands-on enough with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform to take what you design to production yourself.

 - Have built systems behind LLM or agent products, and have opinions about what agents need from infrastructure (state, memory, tool access, long-running work).

 - Have built APIs or SDKs that product engineers loved using: clear abstractions, good docs, and a short path from idea to a first working feature.

 - Have changed a design because of what you saw real users do, not just what they asked for.

If you meet most of these and the work excites you, we'd love to hear from you.




BONUS POINTS FOR...

 - Building safety or fairness controls into an AI  product.

 - Maintaining an open source project other people depend on.

 - Building MCP servers, agent runtimes, sandboxes for untrusted code or LLM gateways, including model routing and cost optimization (we use LiteLLM).

 - Building identity and auth that other products rely on (SSO, OAuth, "sign in with" flows).

 - Building data warehouses or research data pipelines that protect personal data.

 - Working with student or children's data, or in education.




TECHNOLOGIES

TypeScript, Node, Python, PostgreSQL, AWS (EKS, Bedrock, AgentCore), Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, LiteLLM, NewRelic




WHY JOIN US?

 - Real impact: Your work shapes how 100,000+ educators around the world use AI with their students, and much of what we build is headed toward the public domain.

 - Real ownership: You'll help decide how the foundations of Playlab's product work, from how agents run to how educators evaluate them, and help lead their release as open source.

 - Room to grow: As Playlab and our platform grow, so does this role, with significant opportunities for learning and growth.

 - Real closeness to users: We're in schools every week (deep-dive 1:1s, group experimentation sessions, strategic planning with entire districts). Decisions here are grounded in real classrooms, not abstract personas.

 - Mission-aligned team: Join a small, passionate group committed to equity, creativity and joyful learning, backed by the Gates Foundation, Google, CZI and the Schwab Foundation.

 - Flexible work: Remote-first, with autonomy and a strong culture of collaboration.

 - Competitive pay and benefits: Competitive salary, healthcare covered 100% for you and 80% for dependents, dental/vision covered 100% for you and dependents, retirement, Life/AD&D, monthly wellness stipend, home office budget, new laptop, generous time off and opportunities for professional growth.

jobs.title: Reliability Engineering and Quality Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

About the Role

Verkada ships physical security hardware into over 30,000 customer sites and that installed base now spans enough product generations and enough service life that how it fails is a financial question as much as an engineering one. This role answers that.  You will own the reliability models that predict the field failure rate over a product’s lifetime, the warranty data layer the company treats as source of truth, and the cross-functional programs that detect a problem in the field, contain it, and close it in collaboration with internal Engineering teams and the supplier.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires that you be on-site at our office in San Mateo, CA 5 days a week.

What You'll Do

• Own Verkada’s hardware reliability models end to end, including Weibull analysis, regression testing, cohort and mixture treatment, uncertainty analysis, and multi-year extrapolation you can defend line by line.

• Choose the model rather than inheriting it, including infant mortality and wear-out breakdown, and reliability changes across design revisions.

• Define and maintain the warranty rate methodology and the dashboards the hardware organization treats as source of truth across all product lines.

• Run the field quality program portfolio: charters, owners, milestones, risks and proper closure, driving investigations across engineering, firmware, support and suppliers without line authority over any of them.

• Own daily field quality surveillance, separate genuine build and lot issues from noise, and own the containment decision path from signal to stop ship.

• Own the Early Field Failure Analysis program for newly launched products.

• Own the expedited warranty return program and the teardown disposition rules that route returned units to refurbishment, failure analysis, the supplier or scrap.

• Drive down rate of No Trouble Found from warranty returns.

What You Bring

• 5 to 10 years in reliability engineering, hardware quality or a closely related field, at volume.

• Commercial or industrial electronics experience required.

• Real depth in reliability statistics, not exposure to it. Weibull and related lifetime distributions, maximum likelihood estimation, confidence intervals and sample-size limits, accelerated life testing and acceleration models. You can explain why a projection moved, which assumption carried it, and how wrong it could be.

• Demonstrated program management across functions you do not control.

• Bachelors degree in Engineering, Math, or equivalent field.

• Must be willing and able to commute 5 days in office.

Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

• Healthcare programs that can be tailored to meet the personal health and financial well-being needs - Premiums are 100% covered for the employee under at least one plan and 80% for family premiums under all plans

• Nationwide medical, vision and dental coverage

• Starting January 2027, Verkada will match a portion of an employee’s 401(k) contributions based on eligible earnings. Match vests on 2 year anniversary

• Health Saving Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) with tax saving options

• Expanded mental health support

• Paid parental leave policy & fertility benefits

• Time off to relax and recharge through our paid holidays, firmwide extended holidays, flexible PTO and personal sick time

• Professional development stipend

• Wellness/fitness benefits

• Healthy lunches provided daily

• Commuter benefits

Additional Information

• We do sponsor and take over sponsorship of employment visas for this role. If we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa.

Annual Pay Range

At Verkada, we want to attract and retain the best employees, and compensate them in a way that appropriately and fairly values their individual contribution to the company. With that in mind, we carefully consider a number of factors to determine the appropriate starting pay for an employee, including their primary work location and an assessment of a candidate's skills and experience, as well as market demands and internal parity. A Verkada employee may be eligible for additional forms of compensation, depending on their role, including sales incentives, discretionary bonuses, and/or equity in the company in the form of restricted stock units (RSUs)

Below is the annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position, comprised of base compensation and commissions (if applicable).

Estimated Annual Pay Range

$170,000—$215,000 USD

Verkada Is An Equal Opportunity Employer

As an equal opportunity employer, Verkada is committed to providing employment opportunities to all individuals. All applicants for positions at Verkada will be treated without regard to race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law.

jobs.title: (Senior) Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Location: Remote or On-Site (Cambridge, MA HQ) · Travel: ~20–30%; must be able to travel and work across time zones · Works with: Head of Product Management, Sales, Commercial Operations, Vision-as-a-Service (VaaS) Operations

About Fathem

Fathem is pioneering Visual Intelligence™ by bringing molecular structure, biology’s ground truth and its biggest blind spot, into view at scale. Working at the interface of agentic AI, physics, new materials, and robotics, Fathem transforms cryo-EM into high-performance infrastructure that can produce high-quality molecular structures in hours or weeks rather than months.

Cryo-EM reveals how drugs bind and disease works with extraordinary precision, but it remains an artisanal process fraught with failure and requires highly specialized expertise. As a result, drug discovery teams are often forced to rely on either indirect inferences or AI-driven structural predictions rather than direct ground-truth data, reserving cryo-EM for select experiments rather than using it routinely to inform decisions throughout discovery.

Fathem is changing that, turning structural biology into a scalable data engine that supports target identification, mechanism-of-action studies, and generative biologics design. The same structures can also train the next generation of biology-grounded AI models.

Founded in 2024 by Flagship Labs, the innovation foundry of Flagship Pioneering, Fathem is based in Cambridge, MA. Our customers include pharma, biotech, techbio, and frontier AI companies. We are building our commercial team now, and the people who join in the next six months will shape how a new category is sold.

If you want to help build the infrastructure for a new age of biology, we’d like to meet you.

The role

You will be the engine that turns Fathem’s marketing plan into campaigns, events and content that reach customers and fill the pipeline. Reporting to the Head of Marketing, you will execute across events, product marketing, communications, email and digital campaigns, and you will own the logistics that make each one run smoothly.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves getting things done. You will work closely with the Head of Product Management on product marketing, and with the field sales team on the programs and materials they need to win.

What you’ll do

• Execute campaigns. Plan and run integrated marketing campaigns across email, LinkedIn and social, web, webinars and events, from brief to launch to results.

• Run email marketing. Build and send email campaigns and nurture programs in HubSpot, segmented by audience, and improve open, click and conversion rates.

• Grow the HubSpot database. Add and enrich contacts from events, webinars, content and partners, and keep the data clean, segmented and compliant.

• Own events and webinars. Manage logistics for conferences, hosted scientific seminars, customer dinners, webinars and promotions: booths, vendors, shipping, registration, speakers, budgets and follow-up.

• Design booths and event messaging. Work with designers and vendors on booth design, signage and the messaging that draws scientists in at each show.

• Update the website. Keep the website current: new pages, offering updates, news, events, case studies and landing pages for campaigns.

• Create content with product marketing. With the Head of Product Management, create launch plans, messaging, pitch decks, brochures, application notes, blog posts and competitive materials for each offering.

• Build the KOL strategy. Identify the key opinion leaders in structural biology, drug discovery and AI who can champion Fathem, and decide how to engage them: seminars, webinars, co-authored content, case studies, advisory roles and conference talks.

• Support communications. Draft news releases, social posts and customer stories, and coordinate with the PR agency.

• Enable the field. Give sales teams the presentations, collateral, case studies and campaign follow-up they need, and gather their feedback on what works.

• Invest where it pays off. Track KPIs and ROI for every campaign, event and channel: leads, cost per lead, engagement, pipeline and bookings sourced. Use the data to recommend where to put the next dollar and what to repeat or cut.

First-year outcomes

• A steady calendar of campaigns, webinars and events run on time and on budget.

• HubSpot database growing every month in size and quality, with segments ready for targeted campaigns.

• Email programs meeting agreed engagement and lead targets.

• Website updated regularly, with landing pages live for every major campaign.

• Launch and sales materials in place for each Fathem offering, built with Product Management.

• A KOL plan in place, with named KOLs actively engaged in Fathem seminars, content or events.

• Every major campaign and event reported with KPIs and ROI, and budget shifted toward the best-performing activities.

What you bring

• 5+ years of B2B marketing experience (7+ for Senior), ideally in life science tools, services or biotech.

• Proven execution across events, email campaigns, product marketing and communications.

• Hands-on HubSpot experience, including email, workflows, lists and reporting.

• Experience updating websites in a CMS such as HubSpot, WordPress or Webflow.

• Strong event and logistics management, from trade shows and booth design to webinars.

• Experience building KOL programs or working with scientific thought leaders.

• Clear, accurate writing for scientific and business audiences.

• Very data- and KPI-driven, with a clear understanding of the ROI of marketing activities and where investment pays off best. Organized, detail-oriented and able to juggle many projects at once in a fast-moving startup.

• A collaborative style with sales, product and operations teams.

Nice to have

• A scientific background in biology, biochemistry or a related field.

• Experience marketing to pharma and biotech scientists, or to AI/ML audiences.

• Familiarity with Salesforce, LinkedIn campaigns, SEO and design tools

About Flagship

Flagship Pioneering is a bioplatform innovation company that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in generation of over 500 patents, initiation of over 50 clinical trials for novel therapeutic agents and an aggregate value of more than $90 billion. Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com.

Flagship Pioneering is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

At Flagship, we recognize there is no perfect candidate. If you have some of the experience listed above but not all, please apply anyway. Experience comes in many forms, skills are transferable, and passion goes a long way. We are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams and look forward to learning more about your unique background.

Recruitment & Staffing Agencies: Flagship Pioneering and its affiliated Flagship Lab companies (collectively, “FSP”) do not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to FSP or its employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Flagship Pioneering’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of FSP, and FSP will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

The salary range for this role is $121,000 - $176,000. Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate's qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience. Fathem, Inc currently offers healthcare coverage, annual incentive program, retirement benefits and a broad range of other benefits. Compensation and benefits information is based on Fathem, Inc's good faith estimate as of the date of publication and may be modified in the future.

Privacy Notice for Applicants: When you apply for a role at Flagship Pioneering or one of its portfolio companies, we collect and use personal information you provide (such as your name, contact details, work history, and application materials) to evaluate your application, communicate with you, and comply with legal obligations. Cryo-EM reveals how drugs bind and disease works with extraordinary precision, but it remains an artisanal process fraught with failure and requires highly specialized expertise. As a result, drug discovery teams are often forced to rely on either indirect inferences or AI-driven structural predictions rather than direct ground-truth data, reserving cryo-EM for select experiments rather than using it routinely to inform decisions throughout discovery.

Fathem is changing that, turning structural biology into a scalable data engine that supports target identification, mechanism-of-action studies, and generative biologics design. The same structures can also train the next generation of biology-grounded AI models.

Founded in 2024 by Flagship Labs, the innovation foundry of Flagship Pioneering, Fathem is based in Cambridge, MA. Our customers include pharma, biotech, techbio, and frontier AI companies. We are building our commercial team now, and the people who join in the next six months will shape how a new category is sold.

If you want to help build the infrastructure for a new age of biology, we’d like to meet you.

The role

You will take Fathem from an unknown name to a known name in structural biology and drug discovery, and build the marketing function that gets it there. Marketing is expected to generate the majority of the qualified leads our sales team needs to hit its goals, so this is a demand role as much as a brand role. You will think big, try what others haven’t, and prove what works with data.

You will run lean. Fathem is a Flagship Pioneering company, and you will use Flagship’s shared marketing, communications and design resources where they help, and spend Fathem’s own budget only where it moves the number.

You will speak to two audiences with one story. To structural biologists and drug discovery leaders, Fathem rapidly screens targets, binders and conditions at campaign scale to move programs forward. To the AI world, Fathem produces ground-truth experimental structure data at a scale no one else can.

What you’ll do

• Build the brand. Create Fathem’s brand, positioning and messaging framework, and make Fathem a recognized name with pharma, biotech, techbio and AI audiences. Lead launches of new offerings and milestones.

• Generate leads for Sales. Own targets for marketing-qualified leads and pipeline, sized to what the sales team needs to hit its goals. Run outbound and account-based programs, nurture and webinars.

• Own digital channels. Own LinkedIn, social media, email and other channels for awareness and education, and own the website and search engine optimization.

• Own the martech stack. Run marketing automation, web analytics and attribution, integrated with the CRM that Commercial Operations owns.

• Invest in the right shows. Choose conferences across antibody engineering, protein science, structural biology and AI/ML, and make each one produce meetings and pipeline.

• Prove ROI. Report return on every program, event and deliverable, including cost per lead, cost per opportunity and bookings sourced, and move budget to what works.

• Build scientific proof. With R&D and VaaS Operations, turn customer results into case studies, application notes, data releases and customer stories.

• Lead PR and communications. Direct the PR agency, run announcements for financings, partnerships and milestones, raise executive visibility, and help define and hire your first Marketing Manager.

• Work across functions. Partner with Sales on lead handoff and account targeting, with Commercial Operations on CRM, funnel reporting and planning, and with VaaS Operations on what we promise customers.

• Run lean with Flagship. Use Flagship’s existing capabilities where they fit, and bring work in house only when volume justifies it.

First-year outcomes

• One brand and messaging framework adopted across the company, used in every customer conversation and launch.

• Marketing-qualified leads meet the monthly target, and Sales has the pipeline it needs for its number.

• Website, SEO and social channels show steady growth in reach, engagement and inbound demand.

• ROI is reported monthly for every major program and event, and spend stays within the agreed budget.

• Fathem is a recognized name at the key scientific and AI venues.

• Your first Marketing Manager is scoped and hired, and the Flagship, agency and contractor model is running.

What you bring

• 10+ years in B2B marketing in life science tools or services, including 3+ years leading a marketing function at a startup or scale-up.

• A track record of building a brand from little or nothing and creating momentum and interest in the market.

• Strong outbound and demand generation experience, with leads and pipeline that measurably helped sales teams hit their numbers.

• Hands-on command of digital: LinkedIn and social, website, SEO, marketing automation and the martech stack.

• Data-driven and organized, with clear ROI reporting on programs and events.

• Clear, compelling communication for scientific and executive audiences.

• A big thinker who brings original ideas and runs lean.

Nice to have

• A scientific background (PhD or MS) in structural biology, protein science, biologics or a related field.

• Experience marketing to techbio companies or AI/ML researchers.

• Experience at a Flagship company or another venture-backed platform company.

• A track record of launching a new category and managing agencies.

About Flagship

Flagship Pioneering is a bioplatform innovation company that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in generation of over 500 patents, initiation of over 50 clinical trials for novel therapeutic agents and an aggregate value of more than $90 billion. Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. jobs.description:
Clinical Care Coordinator (MA)

Location: Bolingbrook, IL | Initially Hybrid/Remote, Transitioning to Fully On-Site

Job Type: Full-Time | Must Reside Within 30 Minutes of Bolingbrook or New Lenox, IL

Schedule: Monday–Friday | 8:30 AM–5:00 PM

Pay Rate: $22.00–$25.00/Hour

About Jaan Health/Phamily

Jaan Health is a leading AI-based care management company serving healthcare providers. For nearly a decade, the company has leveraged its easy-to-use, proprietary technology to enable health systems, medical groups, and ACOs to deliver high-quality, high-ROI proactive care to hundreds of thousands of previously underserved patients.

Phamily, the company's core technology platform, has transformed chronic disease management with clinically tested AI and easy-to-use technology that enables physicians and care teams to offer high-touch, individualized patient care that has been proven to reduce investment in extra labor and the overall cost of care.  Phamily helps ensure healthcare providers are compensated fairly for providing high-quality care between office visits, while improving the lives of patients with chronic diseases. Learn more at phamily.com.

Job/Role Description

Our team is growing! Jaan Health is seeking dynamic and motivated Medical Assistants (MA) Clinical Care Coordinators to join our care team and will report to the Clinical Operations Manager. They will support the development of patient-centered, team-based care, as well as support primary care physicians (PCPs) and practices in managing their panel of patients using a population management informatics tool. This role focuses on high-volume patient outreach through calls, texts, and care platform messaging, while ensuring accurate documentation and seamless workflow with the care team. In addition, this role will support key operational functions such as member enrollment, staff training, and client operations, bridging the gap between clinical expertise and operational execution.

Key Responsibilities:

• Conduct high-volume patient outreach via phone, text, and digital platforms.

• Document patient interactions and care plan updates in EHRs including Epic and Cerner.

• Support LPNs, RNs and providers with intake coordination, scheduling, and follow-ups.

• Assist with patient education and navigation of care plans.

• Escalate clinical issues to LPNs/ RNs as appropriate.

• Assist with patient onboarding and enrollment processes.

• Partner with client operations teams to ensure seamless delivery of services.

• Identify process improvement that enhance patient and client satisfaction.

• Deliver training sessions on care protocols, systems, and operations to care management teams.

• Adapt to evolving workflows, technology, and program demands.

• Support other operational functions as needed

• Contributes to a positive experience for patients and families through courteous telephone and digital interactions, accurate and expeditious routing, as well as referral to appropriate clinical staff when necessary.

• Perform all job functions in compliance with applicable federal, state, local and company policies and procedures.

Requirements:

• Certified Medical Assistant required.

• Minimum of 3 years-experience in primary care setting or similar specialty. Experience in population health preferred.

• Excellent communication and technology skills.

• Prior use of electronic health records (Epic) and other health care information systems desirable.

• Significant experience within a primary care setting (chronic care preferred, hospital, medical groups).

• Proven problem-solver, comfortable with high-volume outreach, and ability to multi-task.

• Bilingual-Spanish a huge plus.

Work style & logistics:

We are a fast-growing, early-stage company with a bold mission and significant work ahead; every employee at Jaan Health must embody growth company DNA. This means you have proven success in a high-performing environment: high velocity, strong ownership, comfort with ambiguity, resilience, and a true growth mindset.

You are both a playbook builder and executor, able to design scalable approaches for today while anticipating what the business will need tomorrow, and then follow through to deliver results.

Our culture is built on five principles that shape how we work, lead, and grow:

• Care: We care deeply about each other, our colleagues, patients, providers, clients, and communities we serve, knowing that what we do has a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

• Curiosity: We stay curious, are bothered by limitations, and never settle for complacency because yesterday’s answers won’t solve tomorrow’s problems.

• Clarity: We get concrete and create clarity through focused thinking, direct communication, and decisive action so great teams can move fast.

• Craftsmanship: We believe excellence and innovation are habits.

• Commitment: We are relentlessly committed to winning together the right way.

Our Compensation & Benefits:

• Competitive compensation based on experience and impact

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents at a low cost

• Generous Paid Time Off: up to 35 paid days off each year so you can recharge, recover, and give back, including: 12 vacation days accrued annually for rest, travel, and personal time Up to 9 sick/wellness days to prioritize your health and well-being 12 paid company holidays throughout the year 2 Paid Give-Back Days to volunteer and make a meaningful impact in the communities you care about

• HSA and FSA account options

• 401(k) with company match after 6 months of full-time employment 100% match on the first 3% contributed, and 50% match on the next 2% contributed

• A collaborative, mission-driven team helping transform healthcare at scale

If you take pride in delivering results, embrace challenges, and proactively seek improvement, then this is the place for you. You’ll join a smart, humble, and collaborative team dedicated to improving healthcare.

This position is responsible for complying with all organizational security, privacy, and compliance policies applicable to the role, including separation of duties requirements, and for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information and systems they access.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Phamily is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other legally protected status.
