jobs.title: Principal Software Security Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE SECURITY ENGINEER

Based out of Rocket Lab's Littleton, CO site, the Principal Software Security Engineer will be responsible for the development of secure software architectures embedded in our space vehicles, space payloads, and ground systems. Initially, you will work on the company’s most advanced satellite system serving the national security communications needs of the United States.  You will work directly with program leadership as a key member of the software development management team to drive cyber security principles and features into all aspects of the program.  You will interact with company cybersecurity management to develop processes that persist and improve how we build space systems at Rocket Lab.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Design security into Rocket Lab’s flight software suite and program ground and enterprise software

• Work with Rocket Lab’s cybersecurity management team to assess security vulnerabilities, identify mitigation strategies, develop cybersecurity processes that apply across many programs, and document our progress for our customer and internal users.

• Lead the program cybersecurity testing activities, including developing plans for vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and encryption testing.

• Work with Rocket Lab’s mission partners to synchronize designs, processes, and documentation to meet customer requirements.

• Make recommendations on cybersecurity processes and implementation to ensure project objectives are set and roles of team members are clear.

• Proactively manage and communicate risks and issues related to cybersecurity vulnerability, satellite system functionality, and cybersecurity documentation,

• Recommend solutions to conflicts between multiple teams/functions caused by security and cybersecurity. Communicate project progress frequently and effectively to staff and executive levels and work effectively within organization to evaluate development and test results.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related technical engineering field (e.g., electrical or computer engineering).

• 12+ years of software development experience

• 7+ years of direct experience in cybersecurity implementation, operations, and documentation

• Demonstrated experience developing secure applications, preferably for embedded hardware

• Experience working within a Risk Management Framework (RMF)

• Experience developing and maintaining secure coding guidelines and standards

• U.S citizenship is required, due to program requirements

• Active secret clearance or ability to obtain a security clearance

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Master’s or PhD in engineering (software, computer, electrical, aerospace, mechanical, or other technical engineering discipline)

• Understanding of key spacecraft subsystems and their associated components, including: attitude determination and control (ADCS), electrical power systems (EPS), space-ground communications, on-orbit command and data handling (C&DH), and thermal control

• Thorough understanding of the space environment, orbital mechanics, and rigid body dynamics

• Experience with MATLAB, Python, and STK

• Experience with requirement management tools such as JAMA or DOORS

• Experience with satellite operations

• Experience with testing electrical subsystems and assemblies, thermal vacuum or random vibration, and hardware-in-the loop (HITL) testing

• Ability to work in a dynamic environment with competing priorities

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. Final agreed upon compensation is based upon individual qualifications and experience.

Base salary is only one part of Rocket Lab’s compensation package for this role. You may be eligible for company stock, or cash incentives, and can purchase discounted stock through Rocket Lab’s Employee Stock Purchase Program. Employee benefits also include medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage; 401(k) retirement plan options; paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave; paid parental leave; and other discounts and perks.

Base Pay Range (CO Only)

$150,000—$215,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Patient Safety Operations
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

The Senior Manager will provide subject-matter expertise and operational leadership for global ICSR regulatory reporting and submissions across clinical development and marketed/authorized products. The role requires strong knowledge of global pharmacovigilance regulations and the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical reporting rules, processes, system requirements, and day-to-day operational decisions.

• Serve as an SME for global ICSR reporting requirements (e.g., FDA, EMA, ICH) across clinical and post-marketing programs, including interpretation and application of country- and region-specific reporting requirements).

• Translate regulatory requirements into clear, operational reporting rules, including reportability, submission timelines, destinations, cross-reporting requirements, and applicable follow-up requirements.

• Support the configuration, maintenance, and operational use of Oracle Argus Safety, with particular emphasis on regulatory reporting and submission rules.

• Provide day-to-day oversight of regulatory submissions, including troubleshooting reporting issues, resolving exceptions, supporting late or failed submission investigation, and ensuring appropriate corrective actions.

• Provide oversight of receipt, distribution, and submission of periodic and aggregate reports and line listings.

• Manage and support oversight of vendors/FSPs and CROs that perform case reporting and submission activities, including performance, quality, issue management, escalation, and reconciliation.

• Provide oversight of reconciliation and acknowledgement of periodic CRO submission trackers.

• Lead or support management and maintenance of the Master Safety Reporting Matrix, or equivalent document.

• Provide oversight of Submissions Mailbox monitoring to ensure appropriate actions and handling of incoming and outbound correspondence.

• Work effectively in a matrix environment across GPS Operations, Safety Systems & Analytics, Safety Science, Clinical Safety, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Clinical Operations, vendors, and other stakeholders.

• Drive process improvement, identifying recurring operational issues and developing scalable solutions that improve quality, compliance, efficiency, and clarity of ownership.

• Author, revise, and maintain controlled documents, including SOPs, work instructions, and other procedural documentation governing safety reporting and submissions.

• Lead or support development and maintenance of new hire and ongoing submissions training material for submissions team members.

• Lead or support submission and/or submissions compliance process improvement and/or enhancement initiatives.

• Support inspection and audit readiness by ensuring reporting processes, decisions, and operational controls are appropriately documented.

• Provide practical, hands-on troubleshooting and escalation support for complex cases, reporting-rule questions, system issues, submission failures, and other day-to-day operational challenges.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences, pharmacy, nursing, or related discipline.

• 5+ years of pharmacovigilance/drug safety experience, including significant experience in global ICSR submissions across clinical development and post-marketing programs.

• Hands-on experience overseeing CROs, vendors and/or FSP partners, including operational performance, quality, compliance, issue escalation, reconciliation, and corrective actions.

• Strong working knowledge of global safety reporting regulations and guidance (FDA, EMA, ICH) with demonstrated ability to interpret regulations and translate them into practical reporting rules and operational processes.

• Demonstrated experience with day-to-day safety reporting operations, including troubleshooting complex reporting questions, failed or late submissions, exceptions, and operational issues.

• Ability to persuade others in sensitive/complex situations while maintaining relationships.

• An innovative team-player with capacity to be effective in a dynamic, continuously improving, and fast-paced company environment.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills with demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a cross-functional, matrix environment and bring stakeholders along through decisions and change.

• Exercise discretion regarding highly confidential internal and external communications.

Preferred Skills:

• Master’s Degree or higher in a healthcare field.

• 7+ years of relevant experience in pharmacovigilance operational and submission activities.

jobs.title: Imminent Risk (Law Enforcement) Specialist – Overnight Shift
jobs.description:

Our adversarial red teaming, model evaluations, and intelligence collection enable engineering, safety, and security teams to stay ahead of evolving threats and deploy AI systems safely.

Location & Travel Expectations

We are primarily seeking candidates based in the Washington, DC, New York City, San Francisco Bay Area, and Denver metropolitan areas. Candidates hired in these locations will be expected to work from a 10a Labs office at least two days per week.

All new hires will participate in in-person onboarding in Washington, DC, New York City, or San Francisco during their first week. Occasional travel may also be required for interviews, in-person meetings, and other business needs.

About the team

We’re building a U.S.-based Imminent Risk team embedded with a leading AI company. The team reviews and labels content and flags imminent-risk cases for escalation, operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

About the role

You’ll review and label content and flag imminent-risk cases for escalation, working as part of a small crew so you’re never reviewing this content alone.

Schedule

This is an overnight role: 12:00 AM–8:00 AM ET, five nights a week. Crews work either Sunday–Thursday or Tuesday–Saturday, so every schedule includes one weekend night. You must be available to work overnights on an ongoing basis. Occasionally, you may need to switch shifts to cover absences or busy periods.

What you'll do

• Review and label content, and flag imminent-risk cases for escalation

• Apply policy consistently and document your decisions clearly

• Bring edge cases to the senior specialist on your shift on weekdays, or to the client’s designated contact on weekends

• Take part in quality reviews and calibration, and apply feedback

• Hand off clearly to the next shift

What we're looking for

• 2+ years reviewing violent content, credible threats, or violent extremist material in a Trust & Safety, content moderation, or investigative context

• Comfortable reviewing distressing material on a regular basis

• Sound judgment and consistency, including on ambiguous cases

• Clear, concise written communication

• Must be available to work overnights on an ongoing basis, including one weekend night, and occasionally switch shifts when coverage requires it

Nice to have

• Prior overnight or shift work

• Training in crisis intervention or threat assessment

• Background in emergency dispatch, crisis lines, or law enforcement

Content and wellness

This role involves regular exposure to graphic and distressing content, including threats of violence and violent extremism. We take wellbeing seriously and provide dedicated mental health support and wellness resources.

Requirements

• Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or other protected individual) based in the United States

• Must be able to pass a background check

• Cannot currently be a sworn law enforcement officer or employed by a law enforcement or other government agency (former and retired officers are encouraged to apply)

• Reliable internet and a quiet, private workspace suitable for reviewing sensitive content

Employment and compensation

• This is a full-time, 12-month role supporting a client engagement, with the possibility of extension.

• Work Environment: Fully remote, U.S.-based

• Salary: 105,000 - 115,000 depending on experience and location

• Time Off: Generous PTO

• Retirement: 401(k) plan

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Case Management, Global Patient Safety Operations
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Provides operational oversight of end-to-end ICSR case processing across the product development lifecycle, ensuring activities performed by RevMed personnel and embedded FSP resources are conducted in accordance with applicable global regulatory requirements, RevMed procedures, data standards, and established case-processing timelines. Maintains sponsor oversight and accountability for outsourced or delegated activities, including monitoring quality, compliance, workflow performance, and adherence to established processes.

• Maintains operational visibility of the end-to-end ICSR workflow from receipt and intake through processing, quality control, medical review, submission, follow-up and closure, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution of workflow exceptions.

• Monitors day-to-day case-processing workflow health, quality and compliance using operational metrics /dashboards, including case intake/triage, processing timeliness, workflow aging, quality outcomes, follow-up activities, and late or potentially late cases.

• Identifies trends and operational risks and drives timely escalation, investigation and corrective and preventive actions, as appropriate.

• Provide day-to-day operational direction and support to embedded FSP resources; resolve case-processing questions, workflow issues and exceptions; clarify procedural expectations; and coordinate escalation to appropriate RevMed subject-matter experts when required.

• Monitor case inventory and workflow progression from intake through case completion and submission, identifying aging inventory, bottlenecks, quality issues, missed milestones and compliance risks and ensuring appropriate remediation. Identify trends and recurring issues; and partner with FSP leadership and RevMed stakeholders on corrective actions and continuous improvement.

• Identifies recurring case-processing issues and drives process improvement initiatives across people, process and technology to improve quality, compliance, efficiency, scalability and clarity of ownership.

• Reviews and, where applicable, approve case-processing exceptions and controlled case-management activities, including case deletions, case corrections, late-case investigations and other defined operational exceptions, ensuring appropriate documentation, root-cause evaluation, escalation and corrective action.

• Oversees vendor case-processing quality control, including risk-based case sampling, review of quality findings and tracking of corrections to completion.

• Reviews vendor quality metrics and recurring errors, agrees on remediation and training needs with vendor leadership, and monitors the effectiveness of corrective actions.

• Oversees vendor literature surveillance activities, ensuring searches and screening are completed and documented at the required frequency and potential ICSRs are routed promptly for assessment and processing.

• Monitors literature surveillance compliance, investigates missed or delayed reviews and ensures search records, screening decisions and supporting articles are maintained in an inspection-ready state.

• Develops and maintains case-management procedures, work instructions and training materials; ensures FSP resources are appropriately trained, qualified and equipped to perform assigned activities.

• Partners closely with GPS Safety Systems & Analytics to translate case-processing business needs into system requirements, identify workflow or configuration issues affecting case operations, support testing of enhancements and ensure system functionality supports compliant and efficient case processing.

• Leads process improvement initiatives and provide coaching and development to assigned staff; may manage direct reports.

• Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, nursing, or related discipline.

• Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in pharmacovigilance operational activities.

• Strong practical knowledge of global pharmacovigilance and ICSR requirements across clinical development and post-marketing settings, with demonstrated ability to translate regulatory requirements into day-to-day case-processing operations.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with end-to-end ICSR case management, including intake/triage, case processing, quality control, medical-review interfaces, follow-up, reconciliation, regulatory submission workflows and case closure.

• Experience working with or overseeing embedded FSP, CRO and/or outsourced pharmacovigilance delivery models, including operational performance, quality, compliance, issue escalation and corrective actions.

• Strong operational knowledge of Oracle Argus Safety or a comparable global safety database, including understanding of case workflow, data quality, case versioning/corrections and operational interfaces with regulatory reporting.

• Strong problem-solving skills and demonstrated ability to make sound operational decisions in time-sensitive situations involving case quality, compliance or reporting risk.

• Ability to translate business and regulatory requirements into clear operational processes and to partner effectively with Safety Systems/IT teams on system-related requirements and solutions.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear procedural documentation and communicate expectations across internal teams and embedded service-provider resources.

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment and manage multiple competing priorities while maintaining attention to quality, compliance and detail.

• Demonstrated ability to influence and provide operational direction across matrixed teams without relying solely on direct reporting authority.

Preferred Skills:

• Master’s degree or higher in life sciences, pharmacy, nursing, medicine, public health, or a related healthcare/scientific discipline.

• 8+ years of progressive experience in pharmacovigilance/drug safety operations, with substantial experience in ICSR case management across both clinical development and post-marketing/marketed product environments.

• Demonstrated experience establishing, scaling, or transforming a pharmacovigilance operating model to support the transition of a clinical-stage biotechnology or pharmaceutical company to commercial-stage operations, including preparation for and/or execution of a first product launch.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the Vice President of Manufacturing
jobs.description:
About the Company

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

About the Job

Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention. Panthalassa is moving from pilot production into volume manufacturing, and we are looking for an Executive Assistant to support our Vice President of Manufacturing as they interact with our Pilot Manufacturing, Industrialization, Supply Chain, Quality, Facilities, Finance, EHS, Executive, and Creative teams.

Reporting directly to the VP, you will own the VP's inbox, calendar, and daily rhythm, and serve as their eyes and ears across multiple campuses. You will own calendaring, travel, meeting preparation, communications, coordination, and follow-through. The role requires strong judgment, exceptional organization, discretion, and the ability to stay ahead of fast-moving priorities.

The VP’s work does not always fit within fixed processes, and the day will not always unfold as planned. Success requires someone who can build useful systems without becoming overly attached to them, and who can persist, redirect, and adapt without creating friction. In return, the role offers remarkable scope, ownership, and proximity to consequential work, along with the opportunity to be a part of a rapidly growing manufacturing organization.

Your job is to make sure nothing gets dropped: that the VP is prepared for every meeting and aware of how their team is doing. You will anticipate what is coming so the VP's days run smoothly and without surprises. This is a hands-on, high-trust role, and no task is too small.

You may be a career EA, or you may have built the same muscles in another demanding environment. You hold an exacting standard for your work, notice details others miss, and follow through reliably. You combine low ego and high energy with warmth, good humor, and polish. You communicate exceptionally well, handle sensitive information with absolute discretion, and are energized by the pace and variety of the role.

This is a new position, so you will help define how this partnership works from the ground up. This is not a role for someone who needs a rigid routine. It is a role for someone who wants to assist in building systems and take ownership in a fast-moving manufacturing environment. You must be comfortable on the factory floor, working with multiple teams, and making sure safety protocols are in place for anyone who visits the factory.

Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

Responsibilities

• Inbox & Communications: Triage the VP’s inbox daily, flagging what needs the VP’s attention, filing what does not, and tracking what is waiting on a reply. Over time, draft and send responses to lower-priority emails on the VP's behalf.

• Calendar & Scheduling: Take ownership of the VP's scheduling across internal teams, stakeholders, external partners, and other executives, and across Panthalassa's facilities. Reorganize and compress the VP's calendar around top priorities as they shift, and build buffer time between meetings to protect time for travel and deep work. Check in with the VP daily, at the start and end of each day with a running list of items, to make sure each one closes by its deadline.

• Travel: Arrange VP's domestic and international travel including required documentation, last-minute bookings, transportation, lodging, and occasional on-the-ground support. Build itineraries around the VP's meetings and priorities, and make sure the VP has everything needed before each trip.

• Meeting Preparation & Follow-Through: Queue up documents or links relevant to each meeting for quick reference. Capture action items and follow up until they close.

• On-the-Ground Presence: Be accessible and in tune with emergent issues across all campuses during VP’s remote work periods. Take the pulse of the team: how people are working together, stress levels, morale, and anything the VP should know.

• Site Visits & the Factory Floor: Spend regular time on the factory floor and in pilot manufacturing spaces, working alongside multiple teams. Coordinate with other executive assistants and teams to plan and run site visits smoothly, including PPE distribution, safety briefings, and logistics coordination.

Required Qualifications

• 2–3+ years supporting a senior executive, including ownership of inbox and calendar.

• Experience supporting an executive who is not always co-located with you.

• A proven ability to prioritize and protect an executive's time.

• Strong emotional intelligence: you notice how people are doing and can describe it fairly and constructively.

• Absolute discretion with sensitive company, personnel, and personal information.

• Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and follow-through.

• Skill in building clean, useful documents, trackers, and presentations.

• Fluency with Google Workspace, Slack, and spreadsheets, and the ability to learn new software and AI tools quickly.

• Must be comfortable working on the factory floor, coordinating across multiple teams, and ensuring safety protocols are in place for every visitor.

• Willingness to seek, receive, and act on direct feedback.

• Flexibility to respond to occasional time-sensitive needs outside standard business hours.

Desired Qualifications

• Experience in manufacturing, hardware, energy, or another operations-heavy environment.

• Familiarity with manufacturing concepts such as pilot production, industrialization, and production ramp.

• Experience coordinating cross-functional programs, site visits, or events with external guests.

• Experience building support systems for an executive.

The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

Additional Requirements

• Must be based in or near Portland, Oregon, or willing to relocate rapidly (relocation assistance provided).

• Must have a valid driver's license and be able to travel between Portland and Vancouver, Washington.

• Ability to walk and stand on the production floor during site visits and team check-ins. PPE is required in designated production areas.

• Intermittently able to work longer hours and weekends to support critical needs. While we expect a lot of each other, we also offer a high degree of autonomy and work-life balance, including flexible PTO and flexible working hours.

Compensation and Benefits

If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

• Cash compensation of $100,000 - $165,000.

• Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

• A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including: Flexible paid time off Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled) Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

• Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

Location

This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in Portland, Oregon.

jobs.title: Principal Software Security Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE SECURITY ENGINEER

Based out of Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Principal Software Security Engineer will be responsible for the development of secure software architectures embedded in our space vehicles, space payloads, and ground systems. Initially, you will work on the company’s most advanced satellite system serving the national security communications needs of the United States.  You will work directly with program leadership as a key member of the software development management team to drive cyber security principles and features into all aspects of the program.  You will interact with company cybersecurity management to develop processes that persist and improve how we build space systems at Rocket Lab.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Design security into Rocket Lab’s flight software suite and program ground and enterprise software

• Work with Rocket Lab’s cybersecurity management team to assess security vulnerabilities, identify mitigation strategies, develop cybersecurity processes that apply across many programs, and document our progress for our customer and internal users.

• Lead the program cybersecurity testing activities, including developing plans for vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and encryption testing.

• Work with Rocket Lab’s mission partners to synchronize designs, processes, and documentation to meet customer requirements.

• Make recommendations on cybersecurity processes and implementation to ensure project objectives are set and roles of team members are clear.

• Proactively manage and communicate risks and issues related to cybersecurity vulnerability, satellite system functionality, and cybersecurity documentation,

• Recommend solutions to conflicts between multiple teams/functions caused by security and cybersecurity. Communicate project progress frequently and effectively to staff and executive levels and work effectively within organization to evaluate development and test results.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related technical engineering field (e.g., electrical or computer engineering).

• 12+ years of software development experience

• 7+ years of direct experience in cybersecurity implementation, operations, and documentation

• Demonstrated experience developing secure applications, preferably for embedded hardware

• Experience working within a Risk Management Framework (RMF)

• Experience developing and maintaining secure coding guidelines and standards

• U.S citizenship is required, due to program requirements

• Active secret clearance or ability to obtain a security clearance

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Master’s or PhD in engineering (software, computer, electrical, aerospace, mechanical, or other technical engineering discipline)

• Understanding of key spacecraft subsystems and their associated components, including: attitude determination and control (ADCS), electrical power systems (EPS), space-ground communications, on-orbit command and data handling (C&DH), and thermal control

• Thorough understanding of the space environment, orbital mechanics, and rigid body dynamics

• Experience with MATLAB, Python, and STK

• Experience with requirement management tools such as JAMA or DOORS

• Experience with satellite operations

• Experience with testing electrical subsystems and assemblies, thermal vacuum or random vibration, and hardware-in-the loop (HITL) testing

• Ability to work in a dynamic environment with competing priorities

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$173,000—$259,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

jobs.description:

We’re building a U.S.-based Imminent Risk team embedded with a leading AI company. The team reviews and labels content and flags imminent-risk cases for escalation, operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

You’ll review and label content and flag imminent-risk cases for escalation, working as part of a small crew so you’re never reviewing this content alone.

jobs.description:
LA28 does not provide relocation assistance for any positions.

If you are based outside the Los Angeles area, we still welcome your application — we value talent from all geographic backgrounds and want to hear from you if you are able to work on-site in LA.

LA28 is the independent, non-profit, privately funded organizing committee for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. We are on a singular mission to create an Olympic and Paralympic Games that celebrate all that this city and country have to offer, delivering an unparalleled experience for athletes, fans, partners and our community.

The 2028 Games mark the return of the Summer Games to the U.S. for the first time in 32 years and Los Angeles’ third time hosting an Olympic Games and first time welcoming the Paralympic Games. This presents the unique and exciting opportunity to celebrate our legacy with the Games and push the Olympic and Paralympic Movements forward, writing a new chapter of Games history in Los Angeles.

Putting on an Olympic and Paralympic Games is a team sport. To build a Games unlike any the world has seen before, we need the best team in place–a team full of perspectives, experiences and expertise. We are guided by the following set of values and behaviors–optimism, integrity, excellence, inclusion, co-creation and boldness–and look forward to hearing about how your past experiences align with them.

Sport Equipment Manager, Gymnastics

Role Purpose

You will create the field of play for gymnastics at the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games, shaping how every piece of sport equipment is designed, installed, dressed and moved across competition and training venues. Working with the Discipline Manager, Artistic and Trampoline Gymnastics, and colleagues across venue, event and look teams, you will turn International Federation standards into precise plans and dependable delivery. It suits a gymnastics specialist who thrives on ownership, collaboration and visible impact on a historic home Games.

Key Responsibilities

·       Coordinate sport equipment design and installation for competition and training venues with venue, event and discipline teams.

·       Develop the gymnastics bump-in, installation, transition and bump-out work process with the Technical Operations Manager and manage Games-time execution.

·       Coordinate Look application on sport equipment with the Look Team and supplier for World Gymnastics validation.

·       Participate in all Pre-Games IF site visits for Gymnastics, setting agendas and producing reports and presentations.

·       Coordinate equipment installation and removal for Gymnastics Test Activities and manage sport skilled volunteers.

Required Competencies

·       Minimum 5+ years’ experience delivering national and international level Gymnastics events in a leadership role.

·       Extensive Gymnastics and event operations knowledge across professional leagues or teams, federations, universities and grassroots, coordinating with international and US governing bodies.

·       Experience collaborating with colleagues on venue design, event planning, management and delivery across multiple functional areas.

·       Extremely detail-oriented, with excellent organizational skills, strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently to resolve issues.

·       Strong communication, team building and interpersonal skills, and fluency with Office suite tools including Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

Valued Experience

·       Direct experience at a previous OCOG, multi-sport Games or IF level events.

·       Self-starter who defines tasks, seeks feedback and evolves work.

·       Stakeholder relationships that balance assertiveness with diplomacy.

·       A collaborative mindset fostering high performance without ego.

·       Ability to challenge convention and manage change effectively.

What We Offer

·       The chance to shape how gymnastics is staged at LA28.

·       Close collaboration with International Federations and cross-functional LA28 teams.

·       Ownership of sport equipment delivery from venue design through Games time.

·       A team guided by optimism, integrity, excellence, inclusion, co-creation and boldness.

What This Role Means for the Games

Every gymnastics routine at LA28 depends on equipment that is precisely installed, correctly presented and ready on time. Your work will give athletes a world-class field of play and contribute to a lasting legacy for the sport.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

·       Available to work onsite in our Downtown Los Angeles-based office.

·       The majority of work will be conducted in an office setting, requiring extended periods of time using computers, phones, and other office equipment.

·       The LA28 office is an open floorplan working environment; employees must be able to work efficiently in an open cubicle environment.

·       Hours of work may vary, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, especially during peak event periods.

·       Perform other duties as required; the role will evolve over time and may include operational responsibilities during the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

·       Ability to travel internationally to IF and NGB events 1–2 times yearly for 1–2 weeks, under 20% of hours.

Compensation

The annual base salary range for this position is $88,00 - $110,000. The pay scale provided is the range that LA28 reasonably expects to pay as starting base compensation for this role. All LA28 compensation remains subject to final determination based on individual candidate qualifications, experience, or other reasonable criteria consistent with LA28's operational business needs and applicable law.

Accommodation

LA28 is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require an accommodation at any stage, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Equal Opportunity

LA28 is committed to fair and unbiased recruitment procedures allowing all applicants an equal opportunity for employment, free from discrimination on the basis of religion, race, sex, age, sexual orientation, disability, color, ethnic or national origin, or any other classification as may be protected by applicable law. LA28 will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance and all applicable laws. We strive to build a team that is inclusive and encourage qualified candidates of all backgrounds, perspectives, and identities to apply. We assess applications based on relevant skills, education, and experience a candidate can add to our team.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Clinical Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

The Senior Director, Clinical Supply Chain provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for end-to-end clinical supply chain activities across the organization.

Strategic Leadership

• Execute the global clinical supply chain strategy aligned with the company’s clinical development pipeline and long-term business goals.

• Establishes strategies and processes to ensure uninterrupted supply for Revolution Medicines products, comparators and standard of care products supporting RevMed’s portfolio across all phases of development.

• Lead and serve as subject matter expert for clinical supply chain planning, risk management, and execution of clinical supply chain activities.

• Build scalable processes and infrastructure to support early- through late-phase clinical programs.

• Strategic Planning on comparator sourcing management to ensure timely, compliant, and cost-effective product availability.

• Effective management of clinical studies executed in conjunction with collaboration partners.

• Identify and implement overall clinical supply chain best practices.

Clinical Supply Operations

• Oversee end-to-end clinical supply activities, including demand forecasting, protocol reviews, packaging, labeling, distribution, and returns.

• Ensure uninterrupted supply of investigational medicinal products (IMP), including RevMed and comparator products.

• Ensure program related demand/supply is accurately reflected as part of the Development Operations planning (DnOP) process in collaboration with PDM and Clinical Operation team members.

• Ensures efficient global clinical supply chain distribution networks are in place.

• Oversee comparator products demand and supply planning with expert level knowledge in comparator drugs and co-medications sourcing strategy

• Oversee clinical supply chain planning process, optimization of Nside tool for forecasting purposes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner with Clinical Operations and Clinical Study Execution Teams (CSET) in study planning and execution.

• Collaborate with PDM, Quality, and Regulatory to ensure compliant manufacturing, labeling, and distribution

• Work closely with Strategic Sourcing and Business Operations Leads on budgeting, forecasting, and cost optimization.

• Work effectively with internal and external partners to develop sound strategies, identify and mitigate risks, and resolve issues as they arise.

Compliance & Quality

• Ensure all clinical supply activities comply with GxP, ICH, FDA, EMA, and global regulatory requirements.

• Expert knowledge of applicable GxP requirements and applicable regulatory guidance's.

• Lead inspection readiness activities as required for global filings and maintain and inspection ready organization.

Team Leadership

• Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing clinical supply chain organization. Drives for excellence in execution of agreed upon strategies.

• Establish clear performance metrics, development plans, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration.

• Drives excellence in setting clear and actionable team goals.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering or Life Sciences with 12+ years of experience in pharmaceutical supply chain. Master’s degree (MS, MBA) with at least 10 years of experience in pharmaceutical/biotech supply chain.

• CPIM/CSCP certifications a plus.

• At least 5 years of experience in leadership/supervisory role.

• Strong knowledge and experience with cGMP operations for small molecules, end- to end supply chain and demand/supply planning.

• Effective vendor management and oversight skills

• Excellent cross-functional leadership skills with effective communication skills.

Preferred Skills:

• Proven leadership experience hiring, managing and developing teams.

• Knowledge and experience with outsourced manufacturing operations. (CMO’s)

• Effective, open and transparent communication skills (verbal and written). Strong analytical, communication and executive level reporting skills.

• Capable of working on multiple projects/tasks and able to meet timelines.

• Self-starter with a high-level of comfort with ambiguity and complexity and the ability to multi-task while consistently delivering quality results.

• Team-oriented, progressive thinker who enjoys participating in an innovative and creative work environment.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer - Network Software Performance
jobs.description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,

About the team

Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.

Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).

We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.

About the role

For us, performance is a product feature. Customers notice single-flow throughput, packet loss, and latency right away, and every CPU cycle we spend on a packet is multiplied across every server in our network. We're looking for engineers who love finding out where the time goes, and then making it go away.

Some of the things you'd work on:

• Pushing single large flows (e.g., one tunnel carrying a customer's whole data center) to multiple Gbps and beyond, and making that performance consistent

• Finding out exactly where packets get dropped and why: NIC queues, interrupts and softirq, XDP, veth and namespaces, userspace rings, and everything in between

• CPU placement: NUMA, RSS, core isolation, and steering traffic to the right cores on servers that also run many other services

• Cutting the CPU cost per packet in hot paths written in Rust, C, and Go: batching, cache-friendly data structures, fewer copies, fewer locks

• Measuring all of it: profiling with perf, eBPF tracing, and flame graphs; continuous profiling across the fleet; benchmarks in the lab and careful experiments in production

• Building the benchmark and test tooling that keeps performance regressions from shipping

• Helping shape a unified data plane platform so that it's fast from the start

We write mostly Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from NIC configuration and the kernel network stack to userspace packet pipelines.

You'll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our team and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.

We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!

Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience

• Systems programming experience in Rust, Go, C, or C++

• Performance analysis on Linux: perf, eBPF-based tracing (e.g., bpftrace, BCC), flame graphs, hardware counters

• A working model of modern CPUs and memory: caches, NUMA, branch prediction, SIMD, and how they show up in a profile

• Knowledge of how packets move through Linux: NIC queues, RSS, NAPI, GRO/GSO, softirq, and the socket layer

• Experience making high-throughput or low-latency systems faster, and proving it with good measurements

• A solid understanding of L3 and L4 networking: IP, TCP, UDP, and tunneling

• Building and operating large-scale, reliable, distributed systems

• Operating what you build: on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis

• Reading unfamiliar code and safely evolving systems that have been in production for years

• Owning work end to end, from design through deployment, and working across teams to land shared solutions

• Clear written and verbal communication; we design in written specs and review each other's work

Bonus points

• Tuning AF_XDP, DPDK, or other kernel-bypass systems

• Low-latency backgrounds such as trading systems, HPC, games, or storage

• Go runtime or Rust async performance work

• NIC offloads and features (e.g., checksum, TSO/LRO, flow steering, SR-IOV)

• Contributions to the Linux kernel or open-source performance tooling

Compensation

• Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

• For Champaign IL based hires: Estimated annual salary of $168,000 - $210,000.

• For Washington, DC based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $230,000.

• For Seattle, WA based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $230,000.

• For Portugal based hires: Estimated annual salary is between €66,000 - 83,000.

Equity

• This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare's equity plan.

Benefits

• Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S.

• Health & Welfare Benefits Medical/Rx Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Flexible Spending Accounts Commuter Spending Accounts Fertility & Family Forming Benefits On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program Global Travel Medical Insurance

• Financial Benefits Short and Long Term Disability Insurance Life & Accident Insurance 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan Employee Stock Participation Plan

• Time Off Flexible paid time off covering vacation and sick leave Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs.  More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

Cloudflare is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.  We are committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all people and place great value in both diversity and inclusiveness.  All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to their, or any other person's, perceived or actual race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family care status, or any other basis protected by law. We are an AA/Veterans/Disabled Employer.

Cloudflare provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities.  Please tell us if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job. Examples of reasonable accommodations include, but are not limited to, changing the application process, providing documents in an alternate format, using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment.  If you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job, please contact us via e-mail at hr@cloudflare.com or via mail at 101 Townsend St. San Francisco, CA 94107.

• Host networking: classifying each packet once and using that result everywhere on the server, instead of separate configs that can disagree

About the team

Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Our Network Services product suite (Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, Spectrum, and more) puts the connectivity, scale, and performance of Cloudflare's global network in front of customers' applications, network infrastructure, and private networks, providing a single pane of glass for network connectivity, visibility, and network functions like DDoS protection, firewalling, and load balancing. We are a team of engineers and product managers who obsess over quickly building products that solve real customer problems, using techniques that take advantage of Cloudflare's unique architecture and global network footprint.

Our teams build and operate the software behind these products: the data plane that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, the on-ramps and routing that get traffic to and from customers, and the control planes and APIs that configure all of it. We own what we build in production, and a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.

About the role

We're hiring engineers at several levels across a few closely related teams. There's one application and one interview process, and we'll work out with you which team fits your interests and experience. Some of the things these teams work on:

• The data plane behind Magic Transit and Cloudflare WAN, including Unified Routing (our userspace forwarding plane, which gives each customer flexible forwarding of their traffic) and Fast-Path, which uses XDP and eBPF to forward very large single flows

• The on-ramps customers use to reach us (GRE, IPsec, PNI), and the tunnel health checks that move traffic away from failing paths

• An anycast BGP implementation for customer tunnels, where sessions survive being moved between servers and data centers

• Cloudflare Network Firewall, a low-latency userspace packet firewall written in Rust, with rate limiting, intrusion detection, and packet capture

• Unimog, our XDP-based L4 load balancer, which touches nearly every connection into Cloudflare and forwards packets between servers and between data centers

• Spectrum, a TCP/UDP reverse proxy written in Go that brings Cloudflare's network to non-HTTP applications (e.g., gaming, SSH, MQTT, custom protocols, ...), plus TCP Workers

• The APIs and control plane systems that let customers express complex network configurations simply, and that push that configuration to every server in our network

You'll build, deploy, and operate your team's systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our teams and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.

We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!

• Experience building on Linux networking: eBPF/XDP, tc, netfilter/nftables, network namespaces, sockets, etc.

• Experience with high-performance or userspace packet processing (e.g., AF_XDP, DPDK, VPP), software routers, or routing protocols such as BGP

• Debugging, profiling, and optimizing systems where throughput and latency matter

• Building and shipping large-scale, reliable, distributed systems, including APIs and control planes

• Operating what you build: on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis

• Network security systems: firewalls, IDS/IPS, rate limiting, or packet capture

• L4 load balancers or proxies (e.g., HAProxy, Envoy, nginx stream), TLS, or TCP stack internals

• VPN and tunneling implementations (e.g., IPsec/IKE, WireGuard, GRE)

• Building or running networks: ISPs, data center networks, or router and network OS development

• Flow or connection analytics pipelines (e.g., ClickHouse, Kafka)

• Contributions to open-source networking projects (e.g., the Linux kernel, DPDK, BIRD, FRR, GoBGP)

Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,

About the team

Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Companies connect their data centers, offices, and clouds to Cloudflare, and our network carries, routes, and protects that traffic from hundreds of cities around the world.

Our teams build the systems that make those connections work: the APIs customers use to describe their networks, the control planes that turn that into configuration on every server we run, the health checks that move traffic away from failing paths, and the BGP sessions we run with customer networks (the systems behind products like Magic Transit and Cloudflare WAN). We are a team of engineers and product managers who obsess over quickly building products that solve real customer problems, using techniques that take advantage of Cloudflare's unique architecture and global network footprint.

We're looking for engineers who like hard distributed systems problems: keeping state consistent across hundreds of data centers, changing configuration safely while traffic is flowing, and deciding what to do when parts of the system fail. You don't need to be a networking expert; we'll help you learn the rest.

Some of the things you'd work on:

• The APIs and control plane services that take a customer's network configuration (tunnels, routes, health checks) and push it to every server in our network, quickly and safely

• Tunnel health checks that run from every data center, and the logic that reroutes customer traffic when a path degrades

• An anycast BGP implementation where customer sessions survive being moved between servers and data centers, built partly on Cloudflare's own developer platform

• Experimental tooling that catch routing flaps and failures before customers do

• Getting logs and analytics back to customers so they can see what their networks are doing

You'll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our teams and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.

We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!

jobs.title: Senior Research Scientist, Multimodal Deep Learning and Risk Prediction
jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

Join our world-class Research team in the development of state-of-the-art automated machine learning technologies behind Heartflow’s products, including RoadMap, FFRCT Analysis, and Plaque Analysis used to help 750,000+ patients so far. Lead the development and evaluation of problems in Machine Learning and Medical Image Analysis, with a focus on deep learning models that combine 3D medical image data with other clinical data, and on using these multimodal models for risk prediction. Work closely with the Research, Engineering, Data Science and Product teams to develop new algorithms.

Job Description:

• Solving cutting-edge scientific and technical challenges related to developing deep learning models using large-scale datasets, comprising volumetric images and associated clinical data.

• Designing multimodal deep learning models that combine imaging with clinical and other data sources.

• Developing models for time-to-event and risk prediction, matching model complexity and training objectives to the outcome data available.

• Implement and advance on the latest research from the computer vision/machine learning, and survival analysis literature to solve meaningful problems.

• Intellectual ownership and specific lead responsibility related to research, design, and development of deep learning and risk prediction algorithms, including benchmarking against strong, simpler baselines.

• Work closely with cross-functional teams including Data Science, Engineering, Product, Regulatory and Program Management to deploy product-grade ML models.

• Publish cutting edge research and keep up-to-date on latest research trends.

Skills Needed:

• Ability to independently identify project research requirements and design solutions.

• Ability to clearly communicate complex ideas, tailoring content for diverse audiences.

• Strong understanding and proven track-record in machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and/or medical image analysis.

• Experience developing multimodal deep learning models, for example combining medical images with clinical or other structured data.

• Experience developing time-to-event (survival) prediction models, including deep learning approaches.

• Experience working on large-scale complex and/or scientific applications.

• Proficient in Python with PyTorch experience, and preferably also C++.

Desirable Skills:

• Training deep learning models at scale on the cloud.

• Developing deep learning models for FDA-regulated SaMD products.

• Experience building deep learning models for 3D computed tomography data.

• Experience with transfer learning, foundation models or self-supervised pretraining.

• Cardiovascular imaging or cardiology outcomes experience.

Educational Requirements & Work Experience:

• A PhD degree in computer science, engineering, statistics, math or similar technical field.

• 4+ years related experience in Computer Vision, Image Analysis, Multi-modal Deep Learning or related field in academia and/or industry.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary compensation range is $180,000 to $240,000, bonus, and equity. #LI-IB1 #LI-Hybrid

We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.  - Facilitate cross training throughout and amongst teams.

 - Stay informed about industry trends, regulatory changes, and emerging risks affecting operations area, and proactively adjust risk management strategies accordingly.

 - Ability to resolve problems with minimal guidance and make general operational escalation decisions in the absence of the department manager.

 - Ability to interface with other departments, effectively present information and respond to questions from management, team members and customers/partners and operate in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision.

 - Knowledge and understanding of FinTech with a solid operational background.

 - Maintain an understanding of products and services offered.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - Ability to manage multiple tasks/projects and deadlines simultaneously.

 - Attention to detail and accuracy a must.

 - Cooperative and professional attitude.

 - Knowledge of wire transfer systems, payment networks, and regulatory requirements (e.g., BSA, AML, OFAC etc.).

 - This role is a hybrid position and may require you to be in the office.



EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

 - 2+ years previous banking experience preferred with an emphasis in Electronic Payments Processing and/or back-office operations or equivalent experience.

 - 1+ years of experience managing a team.

 - AAP/AFPP/APRP a plus.

 - Be Relentless – Thrive in a goal-oriented environment exercising both patience and persistence. Advocate for our customers and team members and strive to promote the Coastal Difference.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.
