Reporting to the Head of Global Medical Affairs, this leader will establish new functions, introduce innovative approaches to medical engagement and execution, and develop the insights and measurement systems needed to understand and amplify Medical Affairs’ impact.

The role will connect external engagement, medical insights, analytics, digital capabilities, congress execution and launch excellence into an integrated operating model that serves Global, Regional and Country Medical Affairs and cross-functional stakeholders. This individual will help the organization anticipate stakeholder needs, make informed decisions, improve execution and demonstrate its contribution to scientific understanding, clinical practice and patient care.

As a member of the Global Medical Affairs leadership team, the Vice President will be accountable for building teams, processes, technology and governance that can scale with the company’s portfolio and geographic expansion. Success will require translating emerging capabilities into practical improvements in how Medical Affairs works.

This role will partner closely across global, regional and country medical and commercial leaders, Research and Development teams to assess internal and external stakeholder needs and provide meaningful metrics that help Revolution Medicines understand and deliver impact to patients, health care providers, payers and health systems. The individual will also partner closely with Information Systems teams to support optimal design and deployment of tools and systems that make medical teams more effective at delivering impact.

Key Responsibilities

Capability Strategy and Organizational Development

• Define and execute a multiyear capability roadmap aligned with global medical strategy, regional and country needs, portfolio priorities and geographic expansion.

• Build the five reporting functions, establishing leadership, staffing, responsibilities, operating models and investment priorities.

• Assess current capabilities and anticipate future needs across Global, Regional and Country Medical Affairs.

• Prioritize capabilities that improve scientific engagement, decision-making, medical readiness and execution.

• Establish scalable global frameworks with flexibility for regional and country requirements.

• Lead organizational adoption through practical implementation, training, change management and ongoing support.

• Evaluate emerging approaches and technologies, moving successful pilots into sustained operational use.

Global Medical Analytics and Insights

• Establish a global analytics and insights function that brings together medical engagement data, stakeholder feedback, medical information inquiries, congress intelligence and other relevant sources.

• Build a consistent approach to insight collection, synthesis, prioritization and interpretation across Medical Affairs.

• Distinguish actionable insights from individual observations and activity reporting, identifying implications for medical strategy and execution.

• Create mechanisms to route insights to accountable decision-makers and track resulting actions.

• Deliver timely analyses of unmet needs, evidence gaps, stakeholder perspectives and changes in the scientific and treatment landscape.

• Develop dashboards and decision-support tools tailored to global leadership, therapeutic area teams, regions and countries.

• Establish data definitions, quality standards and analytical methods in partnership with enterprise data and technology teams.

• Enable feedback to the teams contributing insights so they can see how their input informs decisions.

Medical Impact and Performance Measurement

• Develop a measurement framework that connects medical objectives, activities, stakeholder outcomes and organizational impact.

• Establish meaningful measures of engagement quality, educational effectiveness, launch readiness, capability adoption and operational performance.

• Complement activity measures with evidence of changes in scientific understanding, identified needs and decisions informed by Medical Affairs.

• Define baselines, targets and review processes that support learning and improvement.

• Help leadership interpret results, including limitations in attribution and the time needed for medical activities to produce outcomes.

• Use analytics to guide resource allocation, identify effective approaches and scale practices that deliver value.

• Communicate Medical Affairs’ contribution through clear, evidence-based impact reports.

Digital Medical Capabilities and AI Deployment

• Lead the digital medical capability strategy, identifying opportunities to improve external engagement, insight generation, scientific information access and internal productivity.

• Partner with Medical Affairs teams to design engagement journeys and channel approaches informed by stakeholder needs and preferences.

• Work closely with Information Systems teams to establish an AI deployment roadmap with prioritized use cases, accountable owners and measurable benefits.

• Evaluate and deploy capabilities such as assisted insight synthesis, scientific information retrieval, engagement planning and workflow automation.

• Partner with Information Systems, data science, information security, privacy, legal and compliance teams to establish appropriate controls.

• Ensure AI-enabled workflows include validation, human oversight, monitoring and clear accountability for scientific accuracy.

• Build digital and AI literacy across Medical Affairs and support sustained adoption.

• Measure realized benefits and refine or discontinue capabilities that do not meet their intended objectives.

External Engagement

• Establish the global framework for identifying, mapping and engaging scientific experts, investigators, emerging leaders and other relevant external stakeholders.

• Build a dynamic approach to global KOL mapping that considers scientific expertise, research activity, clinical practice, professional networks and emerging areas of influence.

• Support coordinated engagement planning across Global, Regional and Country teams while preserving local relationships and accountability.

• Lead global advisory board planning and execution frameworks, ensuring each engagement has a clear scientific purpose, appropriate participants and a defined plan for using the insights.

• Establish standards for capturing and synthesizing insights from external engagements.

• Connect stakeholder insights to medical strategy, evidence planning, scientific content and education priorities.

• Improve visibility into engagement across teams to strengthen continuity and reduce unnecessary duplication.

• Assess engagement quality and relevance using measures beyond interaction volume.

Global Congress Planning and Execution

• Lead the global congress medical operating model, including portfolio planning, resource allocation, logistics, vendor coordination and execution.

• Develop integrated congress plans with Research and Development, global and regional commercial teams, corporate communications, patient advocacy, global scientific communications, medical information, medical training, and regional and country field teams.

• Coordinate planning milestones, stakeholder engagement, meeting support and cross-functional dependencies.

• Establish and coordinate a Congress Steering Committee bringing together senior leaders across the organization to unify our vision and strategy and optimize its delivery

• Work cross-functionally to establish and deliver consistent processes for pre-congress preparation, onsite execution and post-congress follow-through.

• Enable systematic capture and synthesis of congress insights and scientific intelligence.

• Assess congress effectiveness against defined medical objectives, including engagement quality, insights generated and execution performance.

• Build repeatable processes that improve efficiency and allow teams to scale congress participation as the organization grows.

Medical Launch Excellence

• Establish a global medical launch excellence framework spanning prelaunch planning, readiness assessment, launch execution and post-launch learning.

• Serve as a Medical Affairs subject matter expert and coordinate across medical teams to support Global Commercialization Launch Readiness workstreams

• Define medical readiness milestones, accountabilities and dependencies

• Build tools and processes that help teams assess readiness, identify gaps and resolve risks early.

• Integrate evidence availability, scientific content, field readiness, medical information, stakeholder engagement and digital capabilities into launch planning.

• Facilitate launch reviews that give leadership a clear view of progress, material risks and actions required.

• Support country adaptation based on local evidence needs, healthcare environments and launch timing.

• Capture lessons from launches and translate them into improved playbooks and capabilities.

• Partner closely with therapeutic area and country medical leaders, who remain accountable for their medical strategies and local execution.

Global Integration and Cross-Functional Partnership

• Partner with the VP, Scientific Content, Communication and Education to align content and education priorities with engagement needs, delivery capabilities and measurement.

• Work with Clinical Development, HEOR, Medical Strategy and other evidence-generating functions to communicate insights that inform evidence priorities.

• Partner with Medical Information and Field Medical to strengthen insight flows and coordinated scientific engagement.

• Collaborate with enterprise technology and operational functions to ensure medical capabilities fit within the broader company infrastructure.

• Establish clear ownership and service expectations to enable effective collaboration as the organization expands.

People, Resources and Governance

• Recruit, develop and retain a multidisciplinary team with expertise in analytics, insights, digital innovation, external engagement, congress execution and launch excellence.

• Build a culture of curiosity, scientific integrity, experimentation and accountability.

• Develop investment proposals with clear objectives, implementation requirements and measures of value.

• Manage budgets and external partnerships, balancing innovation with operational discipline.

• Establish governance for data use, technology deployment and external engagement consistent with applicable requirements and company policies.

• Ensure the reporting functions operate as an integrated capability organization with shared priorities and transparent performance.

Relationship to Scientific Content, Communication and Education

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Advanced degree in a relevant scientific, clinical, analytical or business discipline; MD, PharmD, PhD or equivalent experience preferred.

• >15 years of substantial progressive leadership experience in biotechnology or pharmaceutical Medical Affairs, including responsibility for building capabilities or transforming operating models.

• Demonstrated success establishing new teams, processes or technology-enabled capabilities in a growing organization.

• Experience working across Global, Regional and Country Medical Affairs.

• Strong understanding of medical engagement, insight generation and the role of Medical Affairs across the product lifecycle.

• Experience developing analytics and performance frameworks that inform strategy and demonstrate impact.

• Demonstrated ability to translate digital and AI opportunities into validated, adopted capabilities with measurable benefits.

• Experience supporting medical launches and major congress programs.

• Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, influence through a matrix and manage complex external partnerships.

• Oncology experience preferred for an oncology-focused portfolio.

Leadership Capabilities

• Forward-looking strategic judgment and the ability to turn ideas into practical capabilities.

• Analytical rigor and skill in translating data into decisions.

• Ability to build organizations and lead change in an evolving environment.

• Strong collaboration, influence and communication skills.

• Disciplined prioritization and investment judgment.

• Commitment to scientific integrity, responsible innovation and meaningful measurement.

• Ability to connect global consistency with regional and country relevance.

• A patient-centered understanding of the purpose and impact of Medical Affairs.

Measures of Success

• Five effective reporting functions with clear accountabilities, strong leadership and scalable operating models.

• Actionable insights that demonstrably inform medical strategy, evidence priorities and execution.

• A credible measurement framework that helps the organization understand and improve its impact.

• Digital and AI capabilities that achieve sustained adoption and measurable benefits.

• Coordinated external engagement informed by stakeholder needs and scientific priorities.

• High-quality congress execution with effective insight capture and follow-through.

• Consistent medical launch readiness across regions and countries.

• Strong partnership with scientific content, communication and education, connecting scientific strategy with engagement and delivery.

jobs.title: Staff Data Platform Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Role

Our AI Search platform runs on search engines, and we are evolving that foundation over time, including moving from an embedded Apache Lucene engine toward OpenSearch. As a Staff engineer, you will own significant features end to end across our stateless search service and the search engine layer, including faceting, deep paging, embeddings, and field-level security. You will work closely with the hiring manager and senior engineers to shape the technical direction of the platform.

What You’ll Do

• Own complex features end to end, from design through production operation, across the search service and the search engine layer.
• Drive search relevancy, text analysis, and analyzer design, which are top priorities for the team. This includes Lucene-level work where it matters.
• Contribute to the design of search backends, including abstractions that let one service run on more than one engine.
• Lead design reviews for your areas. Weigh backward compatibility, reindexing cost, and migration risk before code lands, and require measured evidence for quality and latency claims.
• Keep the test suite reliable. Diagnose and fix flaky integration tests rather than working around them.
• Operate and improve the platform on Kubernetes, with attention to infrastructure and reliability as a second priority.
• Mentor engineers and raise the bar on design and code review.

What you bring:

• 7+ years of software engineering, with a track record of owning complex features in distributed systems.
• Deep working knowledge of search relevancy, analyzers and tokenization, and Lucene or a comparable search engine.
• Strong Java skills (we use Java 21 and Maven) and a habit of writing clear, well-tested code.
• Experience designing features that must stay correct across versions, including index compatibility, schema changes, and rolling upgrades.
• Influence on technical direction through written design, not only through code.
• Clear, direct communication in design reviews, including pushback when a proposal is risky.

Strongly preferred:

• Hands-on experience with a search engine such as OpenSearch or Elasticsearch in a Kubernetes environment, including plugin development.
• Experience with kNN and vector search, embeddings, reranking, or learning-to-rank.
• Experience with faceting, aggregations, or large-result paging at scale.
• Experience with multilingual search, such as tokenizers for non-English languages.
• Experience with field-level security or access control in search results.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer - Space Hardware, Electronics & Test
jobs.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.



With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Own the transition of spacecraft hardware from released design to repeatable, high-quality production. You will develop manufacturing processes, work instructions, fixtures, test methods, and production data systems across mechanical, electrical, antenna, solar, payload, avionics, GNC, harness, and PCB hardware.

You will work closely with design engineering, quality, technicians, suppliers, and contract manufacturers to improve producibility, reduce cycle time, resolve nonconformances, and ensure each unit is built and tested to a traceable standard.







RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop and release assembly, integration, bonding, inspection, handling, deployment, rework, and test procedures for spacecraft hardware.

 - Support build, inspection, configuration controls, and acceptance test plans for electrical and mechanical flight hardware.

 - Design and validate production fixtures, handling tools, breakout boxes, ground support equipment, and test setups using CAD.

 - Define and improve electrical, functional, continuity, alignment, polarity/phasing, and deployment test processes.

 - Automate test execution, controlled test configurations, and serialized-unit data capture using Python, test frameworks, or similar tools.

 - Develop bonding processes for antennas, solar panels, and composites, including surface preparation, adhesive dispense, cure control, and inspection.

 - Coordinate with PCBA suppliers to review completed acceptance testing and records, avoiding redundant in-house testing while maintaining required incoming verification.

 - Maintain and improve MES workflows, mBOMs, configuration controlled build records, and manufacturing change control processes.

 - Conduct root cause analysis for build and test failures; implement and verify corrective actions through closure.

 - Run process dry runs and production readiness reviews; train technicians and incorporate production feedback into released procedures.

 - Track yield, defects, escapes, cycle time, and build data to drive process improvements and DFM feedback.

 - Maintain safe manufacturing and test practices, particularly for batteries, voltage testing, bonding/grounding, and sensitive electronic hardware.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - B.S. in Manufacturing Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Materials Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

 - 3+ years of manufacturing, test, or production engineering experience supporting hardware built to specification, preferably in aerospace, space, defense, automotive, or another high reliability environment.

 - Hands-on experience developing and supporting build, inspection, integration, and test processes for electronic and/or mechanical hardware.

 - Experience using MES and/or ERP systems, configuration-controlled manufacturing records, and mBOMs to support traceability, build execution, and production change control.

 - Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings, GD&T, schematics, wiring diagrams, harness drawings, and assembly prints.

 - Experience writing clear, controlled, step-by-step manufacturing and test procedures.

 - Experience designing fixtures, tooling, ground-support equipment, or test setups using CAD.

 - Experience troubleshooting hardware build or test failures, performing root-cause analysis, and driving corrective actions through closure.

 - Experience with production test, test automation, data capture, or manufacturing process development.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience building automated test stations operated routinely by technicians.

 - Programming experience in Python or a similar language for test automation or data analysis.

 - Experience with antenna/RF hardware, solar arrays, deployable mechanisms, hinges, adhesives, composites, or panel assemblies.

 - Experience with spacecraft GNC hardware, including acceptance testing, handling, alignment, and installation processes.

 - Experience with harness build, installation, continuity testing, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 practices.

 - Experience with PCBA production and test methods, including inspection, conformal coating, staking, underfill, rework, and IPC-A-610 / J-STD-001 requirements.

 - Experience with power electronics, lithium-ion battery systems, spacecraft bonding and grounding, or electrical ground-support equipment design.

 - Experience managing suppliers or contract manufacturers, including incoming inspection, data-package review, corrective actions, and quality-trend analysis.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Production processes are clear, repeatable, safe, and technician-friendly.

 - mBOMs, MES workflows, and build records accurately reflect the released product configuration.

 - Test coverage detects defects early, with traceable data tied to each serialized unit.

 - Fixtures, automation, and process controls reduce setup errors and cycle time.

 - Nonconformances result in durable corrective actions rather than recurring workarounds.

 - Manufacturing feedback improves product manufacturability, yield, reliability, and production readiness.

For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). 



For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).



For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.

jobs.title: Sr. Staff Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
CSQ128R208

PLEASE NOTE: Due to federal contract requirements and client site access obligations, U.S. citizenship and eligibility for a U.S. government secret clearance are required to access classified information. Candidates with an active Secret or higher clearance are strongly encouraged to apply.

About Databricks: At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers and deeply customer-obsessed, we leap at every opportunity to solve hard technical challenges, from designing modern application interfaces to architecting highly available, distributed systems at massive scale. And we're only getting started.

The Role:As a Senior Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), you will be the principal technical authority working with our largest and most complex federal government customers to solve their most critical software, data, and AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will define the technical vision, pioneer novel system architectures, and lead the implementation of enterprise-scale applications spanning backend infrastructure, API integration, and AI-powered product development.

At the Senior Staff level, you are a force multiplier. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering leadership, product management, and developer relations. You will act as a trusted advisor to technical executives at customer organizations, integrating deeply with client codebases and systems while mentoring other FDEs and engineering teams. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for elite builders and technical strategists who thrive at the intersection of software engineering, distributed systems, and massive business impact.

Please note: this role is hybrid and has a requirement to travel to customer locations 20-25% of the time.

The impact you will have:

• Strategic Solution Leadership: Lead the most complex and high-stakes customer technical projects. Pioneer and build robust, first-of-their-kind reference architectures, massive-scale custom enterprise applications, and seamless integrations with cutting-edge AI/ML models.

• Enterprise Transformation: Drive executive-level technical strategy as strategic customers implement transformational software projects. Oversee the end-to-end design, build, and deployment of industry-leading, data-intensive AI applications across highly matrixed federal organizations.

• Visionary Guidance: Act as a trusted technical advisor to C-suite and VP-level customer stakeholders. Guide technical leadership on software architecture, system design, and platform adoption, successfully steering their long-term Databricks development strategy.

• Architectural Pioneer: Own and define software architecture decisions for systems with unprecedented scale or security requirements. Ensure applications are secure, highly available, scalable, and set the standard for modern software engineering and Databricks best practices globally.

• Deliver Technical Excellence: Orchestrate multi-team, multi-quarter technical engagements. Align Databricks technical teams, Architects, and Customer engineering leadership to ensure flawless delivery of mission-critical software components.

• Product Engineering Influence: Partner heavily with Databricks Core Engineering and Product leadership. Translate complex, edge-case developer challenges from the field into actionable product roadmap initiatives, APIs, and platform enhancements.

• Customer Immersion & Navigation: Embed with customer engineering teams, navigating highly complex organizational structures to deeply understand entrenched software challenges and deliver code-level, systemic impact.

• Ecosystem Multiplication: Act as a technical multiplier. Pioneer and open-source massive-scale code accelerators, global development frameworks, and engineering best practices that scale impact across all federal accounts and elevate the entire FDE organization.

What We're Looking For:

Minimum Qualifications:

• 10+ years of experience in software engineering, backend development, or distributed systems engineering, with a proven track record of architectural leadership.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, Applied Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or equivalent relevant years of experience in an Engineering function.

• Expert-level proficiency writing scalable production code in Python, Scala, Java, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript, and architecting solutions using modern application frameworks.

• Deep, authoritative multi-cloud architectural expertise (AWS, Azure, GCP) with the ability to design cross-cloud or hybrid distributed systems.

• Advanced experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and deep internal knowledge of the Spark runtime engine, optimization, and scaling.

• Mastery of CI/CD pipelines, containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and infrastructure as code (Terraform) for complex, high-security production deployments.

• Expert knowledge of MLOps, deploying custom ML/AI models, and integrating LLMs and AI APIs into massive-scale production environments.

• Proven ability to design and deploy performant, end-to-end software architectures that combine backend services, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces with zero-downtime requirements.

• Extensive experience steering complex technical project delivery—managing massive scope, driving agile engineering teams, and translating ambiguous business requirements into actionable, enterprise-grade software solutions.

jobs.title: Clinical Trial Leader
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Tango Therapeutics is a biotechnology company dedicated to discovering novel drug targets and delivering the next generation of precision medicine for the treatment of cancer.

Using an approach that starts and ends with patients, Tango leverages the genetic principle of synthetic lethality to discover and develop therapies that take aim at critical targets in cancer.

This includes expanding the universe of precision oncology targets into novel areas such as tumor suppressor gene loss and their contribution to the ability of cancer cells to evade immune cell killing.

The Tango labs and offices are located at 201 Brookline Avenue, in the Fenway area of Boston, Massachusetts.

Summary

We are seeking a Clinical Trial Leader (CTL) to lead cross-functional clinical trial teams (CTTs) in the execution of clinical trials of Tango’s portfolio. This role will chair the CTT and represent the cross-functional team to internal governance bodies. The CTL will be an internal escalation point for other CTT members.

In a fast-paced, small biotech environment, the CTL will operationally lead the set-up, conduct and reporting of clinical trials as per approved timelines, budget, regulatory requirements, and internal standards. This individual will play a key role in the execution and delivery of clinical trial objectives.

The ideal candidate is highly collaborative, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in a hands-on environment, with a focus on building scalable processes, tools, and best practices to support efficient and compliant clinical trial execution.

Your role

• Lead cross-functional Clinical Trial Team (CTT) in the planning, execution, and reporting of outsourced clinical trial.

• Provide regular updates to internal governance bodies.

• Serve as the primary liaison between the sponsor and CRO to ensure alignment of trial objectives, timelines, and deliverables.

• Oversee CRO performance, ensuring adherence to scope, budget, and timelines.

• Contribute to protocol development and review of key study documents (e.g., ICFs, CRFs, monitoring plans).

• Lead the development of trial-specific plans including risk management, communication, and oversight plans.

• Support site selection and feasibility assessments in collaboration with CRO and internal stakeholders.

• Monitor trial progress through metrics and KPIs.

• In collaboration with Operational Excellence and Compliance, define an optimal RBQM framework to efficiently control quality throughout the trial.

• Proactively identify risks and issues and support the development and implementation of mitigation strategies and action plans.

• Ensure timely delivery of trial milestones including patient recruitment, data collection, and interim analyses.

• Manage trial budgets, change orders, and invoice reconciliation in collaboration with vendor management and finance.

• Ensure study conduct in compliance with ICH GCP, ISO standards, regulatory requirements, and internal standards.

• Participate in audits and inspections. Ensure timely resolution of findings.

• Review and approve essential documents and study deliverables.

• Oversee database lock, clinical study report (CSR) development, and study close-out activities.

• Contribute to regulatory submissions and responses as needed.

What You Bring

• 8+ years of trial management experience with 3+ years in trial leadership position.Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy or related field (required).

• Advanced degree, e.g., MS, PharmD, PhD, MBA (preferred).

• Experience working in global clinical development organization.

• Experience in Oncology development (preferred).

• Direct experience with health authority inspections (FDA, EMA, MHRA, etc.) incl. sponsor GCP inspections (preferred).

• Experience in outsourcing and oversight.

• Knowledge of ICH GCP, FDA guidelines, EU CTR and other relevant guidelines.

• Knowledge of financial planning, tracking, and reporting.

• Knowledge of trial risk assessment and management.

• Familiarity with clinical trial systems (e.g., CTMS, eTMF, EDC, IRT, eCOA) and operational metrics, KPIs, and KRIs.

• Strong vendor management and project management skills.

• Excellent leadership skills with the ability to lead cross-functional teams.

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills.

• Strong analytical thinking and decision-making capabilities.

• Willingness to travel, as required (typically 10–20%)

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

$160,000—$241,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Scientist I, Process Chemistry
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

We are seeking a gifted experimentalist to join our team as a laboratory-based process chemist to own development workstreams for a small-molecule drug substance. You will independently design and execute experiments, solve complex chemistry problems, and develop robust processes suitable for scale-up and technology transfer. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with responsibility for scientific recommendations and delivery of assigned development objectives.

• Own the development of reactions, process steps, or development workstreams, setting experimental approaches and coordinating work to meet agreed project objectives.

• Design and execute experiments to evaluate alternative routes and optimize reactions, workup, isolation, and crystallization conditions.

• Investigate complex reaction behavior and impurity formation using mechanistic reasoning, experimental design, comparison of analytical data, and understanding relevant scientific literature.

• Develop robust processes by defining parameter sensitivity, reproducibility, impurity control, solubility limits, and other practical requirements for manufacturing.

• Plan and execute laboratory studies and translate results into recommendations for process implementation at large-scale.

• Prepare technology transfer procedures and work with external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) to resolve implementation issues.

• Author process development reports and technical content supporting regulatory documentation; maintain complete electronic laboratory records.

• Provide scientific guidance to research associates, present recommendations to project teams, and identify and address laboratory and process safety risks.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• PhD in organic chemistry and at least 8 years of related experience, which may include postdoctoral research.

• Demonstrated ability to independently design and execute process development studies and solve complex synthetic chemistry problems.

• Strong hands-on skills in multistep synthesis, reaction optimization, isolation, and characterization using NMR, chromatography, and mass spectrometry.

• Ability to connect experimental results with process robustness, scale-up considerations, and project objectives.

• Experience taking responsibility for a defined scientific workstream and providing technical guidance to colleagues.

• Clear scientific writing, effective collaboration, and proficiency with electronic laboratory notebooks, data analysis tools, and ChemDraw.

Preferred Skills:

• Industry experience in pharmaceutical process development, laboratory scale-up, crystallization, or technology transfer to CDMOs.

• Experience with design of experiments, automated laboratory reactors, cGMP manufacturing, or drug substance regulatory documentation.

Working across functions and regions, this leader will maintain an integrated view of the external environment and tailor global support to regional capabilities and needs. The role combines strategic leadership and functional excellence with direct contributions to critical business questions as the organization grows. This position is based at our headquarters in Redwood City, CA.

Anticipate evolving business needs and scale support for an expanding portfolio and geographic footprint. Establish an integrated learning and analytics agenda across the three functions, aligning evidence generation and delivery with major business decisions and planning milestones.

jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

As part of our expanding Medical Affairs organization, we seek a dynamic and experienced Director, Stakeholder Engagement Strategy & Operations to support the strategy, planning, and execution of global medical congress activities and elevate Revolution Medicines’ presence at major scientific congresses as our portfolio and organization grow. This individual will report to the Head of Scientific Stakeholder Engagement within Global Medical Excellence and will partner cross-functionally with Commercial, Clinical Development, and Research, providing leadership for global congress activities to ensure seamless integration of congress objectives with broader organizational priorities. Key responsibilities will include:

Congress Strategy & Execution

• Develop congress strategy for Medical Affairs with a focus on oncology therapeutic areas including pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal cancer.

• Lead the strategy to elevate Revolution Medicines’ presence at major global scientific congresses, building a best-in-class congress model that expands our scientific visibility, stakeholder engagement, and impact as the company and portfolio grow.

• Drive development of strategic objectives, overall congress presence, scientific messaging, and engagement plans.

• Ensure high-quality, compliant execution of congress activities including medical booths, satellite events, and onsite pre-congress meetings.

• Lead Medical Affairs planning for global congresses in the U.S., EU, and APAC regions, ensuring global consistency with regional adaptation.

• Assess evolving needs and establish digital capabilities and processes to deliver timely, congress-specific scientific content to external stakeholders while ensuring appropriate governance and compliance across global markets.

• Evaluate and shape congress key performance indicators (KPIs) to optimize approach, priorities, and investments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner with Commercial, Clinical Development, and Research to ensure consistent communication and scientific engagement while maintaining appropriate governance and firewalls.

• Act as the central coordination point for cross-functional teams to align on congress priorities, deliverables, and messaging.

• Collaborate with Publications/Medical Communications to ensure alignment of abstracts, posters, oral presentations, and key data dissemination to other congress activities.

Operational Leadership & Governance

• Provide strategic direction and oversight to agency and vendor partners across congress activities, including booth development, ancillary events, internal meetings, and external stakeholder receptions, with accountability for budgets, timelines, operational excellence, and global and regional compliance.

• Ensure compliance with global and regional regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, PMDA, EFPIA, IFPMA).

• Establish best practices, SOPs, and governance processes for global congress planning.

• Capture and disseminate post-congress insights in collaboration with Medical Affairs Insights & Analytics and the broader Medical Affairs group.

• Advanced degree (MS, PharmD, PhD or equivalent in life sciences preferred but not required).

• 10+ years’ experience in Medical Affairs within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry, preferably within a large, global pharmaceutical organization, with significant oncology experience and a strong background in congress strategy.

• Demonstrated experience leading congress strategy at scale within a global pharmaceutical or biotechnology organization, with a track record of building high-impact, integrated scientific congress presence across multiple functions, programs, and geographies.

• Strong understanding of oncology therapeutic landscape, particularly pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal cancer.

• Deep knowledge of compliance standards governing global congresses and scientific exchange.

• Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional collaboration in a complex, matrixed environment.

• Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills.

• Experience managing budgets, vendors, and operational processes related to congresses.

Preferred Skills:

• Experience in early and late-phase development and product launch preparation in oncology.

• Understanding of global medical congress operations and digital engagement tools.

• Experience working in fast-paced, innovative, clinical-stage biotech organizations.

jobs.title: Director of Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Founded in 2017, Trust & Will is the leading digital estate planning platform, trusted by over one million users. We provide modern, accessible solutions to help families protect their legacies with attorney-approved, legally valid documents tailored to individual state requirements. Our seamless online platform simplifies the estate planning and settlement process, empowering individuals to create wills and trusts while also partnering with financial advisors, attorneys, and institutions to make legacy planning more inclusive and affordable.

As Director of Product Engineering, you lead a team of Product Engineers, and you build alongside them. This is a player-coach role at the group level. You own the outcomes, technical direction, and people leadership across a group of product areas.  You will also ship through agentic systems, set architecture direction, and lead the way with AI on real work and set the example for others to follow. You partner closely with company-wide leadership on what matters most to customers and the business. This is a people leadership role with broad product scope.

About the Role:

• Lead a team of Product Engineers and own the customer outcomes across your group.

• Stay hands-on. Use agents to prototype hard problems and carry complex product work from discovery through launch. Bring in partners for the decisions that need their judgment.

• Share agent workflows that work across teams and coach managers to improve them.

• Work with product leadership to choose which customer problems matter, sequence work across teams and decide what to leave out.

• Meet regularly with members, advisors and partners. Bring what you learn into planning and make sure teams hear it firsthand.

• Help each team ship in small, safe releases, run useful experiments and measure the customer and business results.

• Guide architecture and technical direction across the group with the judgment of a staff engineer, including security and reliability.

• Hire and develop team members and leaders, with clear expectations for how they lead and build.

• Plan the organization, staffing and engineering budget, including employees, contractors and AI tools.

• Use written evidence in performance reviews and calibration, and address problems promptly and fairly.

• Remove bottlenecks that cross teams, and build shared ways of working that last.

Qualifications:

• 10+ years building and shipping customer-facing software, including 4+ years leading engineers and 2+ years leading managers or multiple teams.

• Staff-level engineering depth across user interfaces, APIs and relational data, plus recent work you shipped with agents.

• Experience leading several teams that shipped important product work and owned the results after launch.

• Experience developing managers and senior engineers, including people who took on larger roles.

• Sound product judgment across a portfolio, including using customer and business evidence to choose which work to pursue.

• Experience making product decisions with product and design leaders and guiding architecture reviews.

• A habit of spending time with customers and partners and using what you learn to shape the group's work.

• Care for quality, security and reliability in products that handle sensitive personal and financial information.

• Clear writing and the ability to explain a technical tradeoff to executives and engineers.

• This position is available to candidates residing in the following states only: California (CA), Colorado (CO), Florida (FL), Georgia (GA), Idaho (ID), Illinois (IL), Maryland (MD), New Jersey (NJ), New York (NY), North Carolina (NC), Pennsylvania (PA), Tennessee (TN), Texas (TX), Vermont (VT), Nevada (NV), Utah (UT)

How We Work: AI-Native

• Use agent teams for discovery, research, planning and prototyping. Check speed, quality and cost on real work before asking teams to adopt a workflow.

• Help managers and their teams learn through pairing, shared tools and work they can review.

• Work with teams to turn promising prototypes into plans they can ship safely.

• In the interview, you'll walk us through an outcome you delegated to agents and a workflow other teams adopted.

Bonus Points for:

• Experience in regulated or high-trust products, such as financial services, legal, insurance or health.

• Founder, founding engineer or early product engineer experience.

• Experience in product management or running customer discovery.

• Experience leading an engineering group through a change in how it builds.

• Experience working on high-autonomy, remote-first teams where problems arrive loosely defined.

What Success Looks Like:

• Teams deliver on shared priorities, and the group's customer and business metrics improve.

• Customer and partner feedback changes what teams prioritize, and product leaders can explain why the group chose one investment over another.

• Teams across the group can test, monitor and roll back what they ship, with clear ownership when something breaks.

• Teams review and document architecture decisions, and shared decisions make the platform easier to build on across the group.

• You still ship product work with agents. Managers and engineers adopt practices they saw work on those projects.

• Managers build alongside their teams, and AI Levels rise across the group while quality holds.

• Managers and senior engineers take on broader responsibilities. Engineers across the group get consistent, specific feedback on where they stand and how to grow.

• Staffing and spending across the group reflect its product priorities. You can explain the tradeoffs when those priorities change.

Full-time Employee Benefits & Perks:

• Compensation: Salary + Equity

• Our salary range for this position is $225,000 - $330,000, in addition to compensation we also include an employee equity package as a component of our offer along with other benefits and perks outlined below.

• PTO

• Flexible time off that you are encouraged to use

• Generous paid company holidays and breaks throughout the year

• Monthly friends & family day

• Health and Wellness Benefits

• Exceptional health benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance - we cover 100% of premiums for employees and dependents on medical coverage

• Mental health support through Spring Health, plus access to One Medical for primary care and Cleo for family planning and caregiving

• Financial wellness benefits (unlimited 1:1 sessions with a UBS financial coach and employer-sponsored 401k with up to 4% company match)

• Extra

• Flexible work schedule + hours

• Family-friendly work environment. We support the complexity of a remote world with the needs of families

• Up to $1,000 annually in learning & development reimbursement

• Optional company-sponsored events and travel throughout the year

• $500 Work from home stipend + Apple accessories

About Trust & Will:

• We are a remote-first company, giving our employees the flexibility they need to work in an environment that best suits their needs. Our hiring process is also conducted virtually unless otherwise noted. We are a company that was founded in San Diego, CA, and offer a collaborative co-working space that is available for you to use if you'd like but not required. #LI-Remote

• We are proud to be a certified B Corporation, using business as a force for good. We are committed to building a healthy, sustainable, and engaging working environment for all employees, their families, and communities. We publish an annual impact report to outline our positive contributions to our world and set an example for all employers.

• Trust & Will's mission is to help every family leave their legacy through affordable, accessible estate planning. That starts with the people we hire and the ways in which we support the development of their unique talents and capabilities. We are committed to prioritizing ways to make our company and industry more inclusive. This means we must be revolutionary in the way we value diversity to revolutionize our business sector. At Trust & Will, everyone has a seat at the table and space to be their authentic selves because only in a company that is inclusive and diverse can we truly stand in our members' shoes.

California Privacy Notice: Trust & Will collects personal information from applicants including identifiers, professional/employment history, and education information to evaluate qualifications and communicate about your application. California residents have the right to know what information we collect, request a copy, correct inaccuracies, or request deletion (subject to exceptions). To exercise these rights, contact legal@trustandwill.com. For more information, visit our privacy policy.

Trust & Will may use AI tools to assist with administrative recruiting tasks. All final hiring decisions are made by people. For accommodations, contact people-ops@trustandwill.com.

jobs.title: Senior Global Supply Manager, Raw Materials
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring an experienced professional to own the development and execution of Form’s global supply chain strategy for an array of critical battery raw materials used in Form’s pioneering iron-air battery systems. This role reports to the Manager, Global Supply Management (“GSM”) for Active Battery Materials. As part of the “Actives” team, you will establish and execute on Form’s commercial-scale sourcing strategy, owning our holistic supply strategy for key metal raw materials like copper, steel, aluminum, and more. You will deliver shrewd insights based on a deep understanding of upstream manufacturing processes, market trends, and Form’s requirements, ensuring delivery of quality materials that meet Form’s bold performance, cost, and timeline needs.



The successful candidate will rely on their combination of business acumen, technical depth, innate curiosity, and experience across raw materials categories to bring strategic approaches and oversight to the sourcing of these critical components, while developing and maintaining positive, productive relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners alike. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with a breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own the metal raw materials category at Form (e.g., copper, steel, aluminum), including commercial relationships and contracts within our supply base and value chain

 - Monitor current category market conditions, evaluating capacities and competitive landscapes, technology roadmaps and supply challenges & opportunities

 - Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Supplier Industrialization, Manufacturing, and Leadership to define and drive execution of Form’s sourcing strategy

 - Negotiate and deliver favorable commercial terms that optimize costs, lead times, and risk

 - Ensure Form is working with best-in-class suppliers and mitigating risks by managing the end-to-end sourcing process from supplier identification through RFP, business award, and continuous improvement

 - Secure best-in-class pricing through detailed price analysis and negotiations, continual cost reductions, cost avoidance, and logistics optimization




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelors or Masters degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, or similar discipline

 - 5+ years of relevant category experience in battery raw materials, carbons, or resins, including relevant manufacturing methods and market/pricing dynamics

 - 5+ years of sourcing experience including supplier management, running RFX’s, and driving continuous improvement, in a fluid, fast-paced, manufacturing environment

 - Strong analytical skills, with a demonstrated ability to generate bottom-up “should-cost” models based on an understanding of manufacturing processes; strong with spreadsheets

 - Solid understanding of commercial terms, contract structures, and IP concepts

 - Excellent communication and organizational skills, ability to ruthlessly prioritize across multiple tasks and projects

 - Ability to work in the US and travel globally as necessary, up to 30%
   
   
   

#LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will never solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
🧠 About Cortex
Cortex is the Engineering Operations Platform - mission control for the AI software factory. As AI multiplies how much teams ship, code stops being the bottleneck and everything around it becomes the constraint. Cortex gives engineering organizations the visibility, governance, and golden paths to move fast without runaway risk to reliability and security - across Catalog and Context Graph, Scorecards, Engineering Intelligence, Self-Service and Workflows, and AI Impact. We’re a YC company, SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 certified, used by teams like Rapid7, Xero, BigCommerce, Skyscanner, LetsGetChecked, and H&R Block.

AI-augmented engineering is the floor here, not a side experiment - Cortex engineers build on Cortex every day.

📍Location
We’re fully remote and welcome candidates from anywhere in the US! We have all-company offsites a few times a year where we fly the whole team out to meet in person, build stronger relationships, kick off important projects, and have fun!

🤝 The Team
We are a mighty group of passionate individuals excited about building a product that developers love. We’re a Series C company backed by Scale Ventures, Sequoia, IVP, and others. You can read more about it here.

💼 Role Summary

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead one of our engineering teams and own its delivery, health, and growth. You’ll co-own the team’s roadmap with your Product Manager, step into the code when the team needs it, and be accountable for your team’s outcomes and operational excellence.

🛠️ Responsibilities

• Run 1:1s, growth plans, performance, and team health, and develop engineers at every level, including growing Senior engineers into Leads

• Step into the code when the team needs support, from reviews and fixes to unblocking work at risk, while keeping the team’s overall delivery your first priority

• Drive and support AI-augmented engineering on your team, helping engineers adopt AI tools and workflows and keeping review standards high

• Co-own the team roadmap with your Product Manager: turn the mission into a quarterly plan, plan capacity honestly, and push back on scope that doesn’t match what customers need

• Deliver predictably against commitments and own at least one team-level metric

• Own operational excellence for your team, including incident response, on-call sustainability, Scorecard health, and closing the loop with CX on customer escalations

• Act as hiring manager for your team and reliably hire Senior-and-above engineers

• Run your team on Cortex and feed what works, and what doesn’t, back into the product

✔️Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent work experience

• Experience leading an engineering team, either as an Engineering Manager or as a Lead or Staff engineer who has grown other engineers to the next level

• Able to be hands-on with AI assistance in a modern backend stack, while understanding the code that gets produced

• Fluent, critical use of AI in day-to-day engineering, reviewing AI output as carefully as a teammate’s PR

• Experience owning production systems, on-call, and incident follow-through

• Strong partnership with Product, and able to explain the customer use case behind each feature

• Clear, concise written communication and a pragmatic approach over shiny tech

• Experience at a B2B SaaS company, or in engineering operations, platform, or developer experience, is a plus

• Previous experience at a hyper-growth startup is a plus

💰 Compensation

• Starting Salary Range: $200,000 to $260,000

• Competitive Equity Package

*Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role is eligible for equity and benefits.

🌴 Perks & Benefits

• National medical, dental & vision insurance (we cover 100% for employees!)

• Unlimited PTO & flexible working hours

• 401k plan

• Gender-neutral parental leave

jobs.description:

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

jobs.title: FP&A Manager, Commercial & Marketing
jobs.description:
Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

About the Role:

We are looking for an experienced, highly analytical, and strategic Manager, FP&A to join our Finance team as a key business partner supporting our Commercial and Marketing organizations. In this role, you will act as a trusted advisor to senior commercial and marketing leadership, translating operating plans, go-to-market strategies, and marketing investments into actionable financial models, expense forecasts, and strategic insights.

Focusing on operating expenses, headcount planning, and investment efficiency, you will lead end-to-end financial planning, forecasting, and performance management for all GTM spend. As an advanced professional with an AI first mindset, you will bring specialized depth in headcount and capacity modeling, expense optimization, marketing spend ROI metrics, and cross-functional strategy.

This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our San Francisco HQ office 3 days per week.

Impact You’ll Own:

• Strategic Business Partnering: Serve as the primary FP&A business partner to Commercial (Sales, Customer Success, GTM) and Marketing leaders, providing in-depth financial analysis and strategic guidance on OpEx investments, headcount allocation, and marketing ROI.

• Advanced Expense Modeling: Build, refine, and own complex, multi-driver financial models for GTM OpEx, headcount, sales ramp/capacity planning, and marketing program spend.

• OpEx Forecasting & Long-Term Planning: Lead recurring forecasting cycles, annual budgeting, and long-range strategic planning for all Commercial and Marketing operating expenses. Conduct sensitivity analyses, scenario planning, and variance analysis (Actuals vs. Budget/Forecast).

• Marketing & GTM Investment Efficiency: Analyze and benchmark GTM investment efficiency metrics, including Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) spend components, Cost Per Lead (CPL), payback period efficiency, and marketing campaign spend performance.

• Executive Reporting & Communication: Synthesize complex financial and operational expense data into clear strategic narratives, executive dashboards, and board deck inputs for senior leadership.

• Cross-Functional Process Leadership: Direct the application of financial principles and lead cross-functional projects across Sales Ops, Marketing Ops, Accounting, and Finance to streamline GTM expense workflows, improve budget visibility, and optimize financial systems.

• Month-End Close & Controls: Partner closely with Accounting during the close process to review vendor accruals, marketing program spend to ensure reporting integrity and accurate variance explanations.

• KPI & Metric Standardization: Establish, track, and benchmark critical Commercial and Marketing expense KPIs to highlight spend risks, identify cost efficiencies, and propose proactive solutions.

What You Bring:

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a quantitative field.

• 6+ years of relevant FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience, with a heavy focus on supporting Commercial and Marketing organizations (SaaS or high-growth tech industry experience preferred).

• Advanced expertise in sales capacity/ramp modeling, dynamic OpEx and headcount modeling, commission plan finance tracking, and GTM metrics.

• Track track record of evaluating variable, complex data sets to solve unstructured business problems under minimal supervision.

• Superior communication skills with an ability to influence senior cross-functional leaders, adapt delivery style, and present complex financial insights clearly.

• Ability to manage broad, multi-faceted projects simultaneously, set deadlines, and lead cross-departmental initiatives.

What Makes You Stand Out:

• Deep hands-on experience with modern ERPs (NetSuite), enterprise BI/CPM planning tools (Pigment, Anaplan, Adaptive), and CRM/Sales tools (Salesforce).

• Advanced expertise evaluating digital marketing spend, demand-generation unit economics, and campaign attribution cost structures.

• Experience operating in a dynamic, high-growth technology environment with an agile approach to problem-solving.

• CFA, CPA, MBA, or similar professional qualification.

Application Deadline:

11:45p / 23:45 PT on the date stated below. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. This posting may be removed earlier than projected if a suitable pool of applications has been received. For this reason, we recommend applying as soon as you are able to.

Benefits While Working at Planet:

We’re dedicated to helping the whole Planet, and to do that we must strive to represent all of it within each of our offices and on all of our teams. That’s why Planet is guided by an ultimate north star of Belonging—dreaming big as we approach our ongoing work.  If this job intrigues you, but you’re thinking you might not have all the qualifications, please... do apply!  At Planet, we are looking for well-rounded people from around the world who can contribute to more ways than just what is listed in this job description.  We don’t just fill positions, we aspire to fulfill people’s careers, most excited about folks who are motivated by our underlying humanitarian efforts.  We are a few orbits around the sun before we get to where we want to be, so we hope you’re excited to come along for the ride.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Portfolio Operations Excellence
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Reporting directly to the Senior Director, National Portfolio Field Excellence, the Associate Director, National Portfolio Field Excellence leads the team responsible for Revolution Medicines’ U.S. commercial regional congress, sponsorship, peer-to-peer speaker program, and speaker contracting operations across the portfolio. This leader drives the operating model that underpins these programs- intake, governance, vendor management, budget stewardship, and compliance- enabling brand and field teams to execute with speed, consistency, and confidence in preparation for anticipated launches and in line brands.

This is a portfolio-level position rather than an asset-specific one. It requires a leader who combines people management with hands-on operational and field sales expertise: directing day-to-day execution, building scalable processes in advance of launch demand, and serving as the organization’s subject matter expert on operations supporting regional congresses and peer-to-peer education.

The role also supports planning and execution of national, area, and regional field meetings, including launch and plan-of-action meetings. This includes coordinating timelines, logistics, vendors, budgets, and follow-through, and supporting portfolio-level connectivity across field teams.

The Associate Director serves as a strategic and operational partner to Marketing, Sales Leadership, Medical Affairs, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Finance, Accounts Payable, IT, and external agencies, establishing consistent ways of working and advancing continuous improvement across the U.S. National Portfolio Field Excellence organization.

This is a non-demand-generating leadership role: it carries no sales quota and conducts no promotional activity with customers.

Key responsibilities include:

• Lead, coach, and develop the program and operations team, setting priorities, service expectations, and accountability for execution.

• Lead U.S. promotional speaker bureau operations across portfolio brands, including speaker nomination, vetting, fair market value review coordination, contracting, onboarding, training logistics, recertification, and utilization monitoring.

• Manage speaker program systems and vendors, including field requests, approval workflows, attendee records, honoraria and expense payments, program closeout, and data readiness for Open Payments reporting.

• Plan and execute commercial regional congresses and sponsorships with Marketing, Sales Leadership, and Medical Affairs, including annual calendars, engagement plans, exhibits, field staffing, logistics, on-site operations, and follow-up.

• Manage national, area, and regional field meetings, including launch and plan-of-action meetings; coordinate timelines, logistics, and follow-through.

• Coordinate forums and activities that strengthen portfolio connectivity across field teams in support of shared customers, launches, and evolving commercial priorities.

• Own agency and supplier performance, scopes of work, program budgets, forecasts, accruals, reconciliation, and financial closeout in partnership with Procurement and Finance.

• Establish consistent processes for program intake, approvals, contracting, purchase orders, payments, and documentation; partner with Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance to maintain appropriate controls and practical guidance.

• Partner with Sales Operations & Analytics and IT on systems, workflows, data quality, and reporting; use program results and stakeholder feedback to resolve issues and improve execution.

• Support launch readiness and continuous improvement by building scalable processes, vendor capacity, job aids, and stakeholder training aligned with portfolio priorities.

• Travel approximately 25% for regional congresses, speaker training events, commercial meetings, and home office collaboration.

• Other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor’s degree required with at least 8 years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology sales, commercial operations, including speaker bureau and congress or event operations in partnership with brand marketing.

• Experience leading and developing program or operations professionals, with clear accountability for team priorities, execution, and performance.

• Experience managing agencies and suppliers, including RFPs, scopes of work, budgets, forecasting, accruals, and reconciliation.

• Working knowledge of speaker program and event management systems, or speaker bureau vendor platforms, and related CRM workflows and data flows.

• Strong understanding of U.S. pharmaceutical requirements and company controls governing promotional programs, HCP engagement, and commercial sponsorships.

• Demonstrated ability to improve cross-functional processes from design through implementation, stakeholder adoption, and measurement of results.

• Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and use operational data to recommend action.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to influence cross-functional partners and translate complex requirements into practical guidance.

• Collaborative, detail-oriented, and comfortable building processes and managing ambiguity in a growing commercial organization.

Preferred Skills:

• Oncology experience, including product launch or portfolio expansion.

• Experience planning and executing national, area, or regional sales meetings, including launch or plan-of-action meetings.

• Experience building commercial program processes and infrastructure from pre-launch through launch in a smaller, growing biotechnology company.

• Experience transitioning speaker bureau or congress operations between externally supported and internally managed models.

• Advanced degree or relevant process improvement or meeting management certification, such as Lean Six Sigma or Certified Meeting Professional (CMP).
